questions.question: Did Arnold say those struck by the final hailstones miss judgment?

answers.summary: Arnold says everyone comes to judgment. He places the hailstones at the end of this earth age and says the change to spiritual bodies means those bodies are not harmed by them.

questions.question: Did Arnold say which insects and worms would be present in heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold did not give a definite list. He emphasized the changed conditions of Isaiah 11, including animals no longer being carnivorous, and acknowledged limits to what he could infer.

questions.question: Did Arnold see jury duty as forbidden judging?

answers.summary: Arnold approved jury service as a biblical responsibility, describing peers deciding from facts and corroborating witnesses. He distinguished that task from the spiritual judgment he told listeners to leave to God. This is his religious answer, not legal advice.

questions.question: Did Arnold support adult baptism after infant baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold said someone who felt personally led to baptism as an adult should pursue it. He emphasized its personal character.

questions.question: Did Arnold support an unmarried mother dedicating her child to God?

answers.summary: Arnold answers positively and says a parent’s sin is not placed on the child, referring to Jeremiah 31:29. The other recalled legal reference is uncertain and not supplied as precise documentation.

questions.question: Did Arnold support children being baptized in another Christian church?

answers.summary: Arnold says yes when the children understand baptism as publicly affirming Christ’s death and resurrection. He says one Christian can baptize another and encourages the parent’s support.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that a child lost before birth is born into this earth age again?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no. He says the spirit is already present and that a person passes through this earth age only once.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that a person’s final destiny is fixed at birth?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected a fixed heaven-or-hell assignment at birth. He emphasized decisions, faith and actions under free will and claimed that God had not already determined every person’s response. This is his theological position.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that all people descend from Adam and Eve?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and appeals to separate creation days and the genealogies of Genesis 4–5. His claimed scientific support is not independently established here; the entry records his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that angels can read a person’s mind?

answers.summary: Arnold said neither angels nor Satan can read minds; he reserved that knowledge to God. He then emphasized that God’s complete knowledge makes his judgment fair, including reward for faithful service.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that antichrist would come from the tribe of Dan?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that teaching, identifying antichrist with Satan rather than an ordinary member of Dan. He appealed to Ezekiel 28 and 2 Thessalonians 2.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that apostles or ministers must remain unmarried?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no, points to Peter’s mother-in-law in Mark 1:30 and says some teachers were married while others were not. He also discusses Aquila and Priscilla as married teachers.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that every soul will be saved during the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected universal salvation, distinguished spiritual bodies from mortal or immortal souls in his interpretation, and referred to Revelation 20’s final judgment. He also said listeners must not decide individual destinies. The question’s five-month premise after seeing Christ was not clearly resolved in this response.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that God sends curses or burdens on people?

answers.summary: Arnold uses Jeremiah 23:33 to distinguish God lifting burdens from people bringing trouble on themselves. He says God may withdraw intervention and rejects the idea that another person can place a spiritual curse on a Christian.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that Jesus was a vegetarian?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that claim, referred to the fish account in John 21 and distinguished someone choosing vegetarianism from claiming Jesus practiced it. He qualified his approval of meat with his clean-food interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that Jesus was physically married?

answers.summary: Arnold denied a physical marriage and interpreted betrothal and marriage language spiritually. He also treated God’s divorce imagery for Israel as analogy, referring tentatively to Jeremiah 3:7 or 8. His account of unnamed writings and translators is attributed rather than independently verified.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that Noah’s flood covered the whole earth?

answers.summary: Arnold says it probably did not cover the whole world. He explains its extent through his interpretation of its purpose in Genesis 6.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people communicate in paradise?

answers.summary: Arnold answered yes and said people recognize family members who have died. He described the departed as alive with the Father despite bodily death and referred to communication on both sides of paradise.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people in his first earth age lacked souls?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that premise, saying every living person has a soul. He explained Satan stealing souls as deception drawing people from God rather than removing the existence of a soul.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people killed one another in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no because he describes them as spiritual beings whose final destruction only God can cause. He refers to Matthew 10:28.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that spiritual bodies reproduced in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold answers that there were no reproductive organs in that age and distinguishes it from this age and his account of fallen angels. This is his theological explanation rather than a verified biological description.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell a beer drinker to stop seeking God?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected telling the listener to stop seeking God. He criticized judgmental treatment, advised forgiving the person and also told the listener to exercise self-control and represent God well.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell a child Christ would return when the child turned thirteen?

answers.summary: Arnold gave no such date and said only the Lord knows the time. He did not know the child’s current age from the letter.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell a parent to tithe on child-support payments?

answers.summary: Arnold said no because that money was for the child’s needs. For a financially stretched single parent unable to give a full tenth, he suggested an offering after expenses while leaving the decision with her. This records his ministry advice.

questions.question: Did Arnold think a deceased person from the wrong side of the gulf would comfort someone dying?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively said probably not, then warned the listener not to judge which side someone occupied. The reported medical circumstances are unclear in the captions; neither a visitation nor its cause is independently verified by this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold think a person in heaven would have regrets?

answers.summary: Arnold gives his opinion that someone who makes it to heaven would be happy rather than regretful. He labels this as his own opinion.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Cain knew who his father was in Arnold’s serpent-seed interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold said probably not, emphasizing innocence. He repeated his interpretation of Genesis 3–4 but did not claim direct evidence of Cain’s personal knowledge.

questions.question: Did Arnold think God needed bodyguards because he was afraid?

answers.summary: Arnold denied that God was afraid and described Michael and Gabriel as trusted servants maintaining order and discipline. He said they had not needed flesh birth and connected God’s power with his interpretation of Ezekiel 39. These are his doctrinal claims.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Jesus died on a cross or a stake?

answers.summary: Arnold argued for a Roman cross on the basis of Roman responsibility for the execution and his reading of Psalm 22. He acknowledged differing discussions of the Greek terms but did not conduct a detailed historical comparison in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Jesus remembered his Father as a child?

answers.summary: Arnold said his thought was yes, citing Jesus’ wisdom at twelve and the Spirit’s presence in the infancy account. He did not separately explain why ordinary people do not remember a prior existence. His distinction remains attributed belief.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Michael and Gabriel had lived through flesh life?

answers.summary: Arnold answered no and repeatedly labeled his explanation opinion. He speculated that their earlier service made flesh life unnecessary, without claiming documentation of what they accomplished.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Revelation 17’s ten kings could be rulers of countries?

answers.summary: Arnold answered that these were rulers in the final generation and said that identification was possible, rather than naming specific leaders.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Satan could confuse or possess God?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured the eight-year-old that an evil spirit could not confuse God, describing God as supreme and supernatural.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Satan could freely cross paradise’s gulf?

answers.summary: Arnold denied that Satan or anyone else could cross the gulf at that time. He recommended Luke 16, distinguished Job 1:6’s earlier freedom from his belief in Michael’s present restraint, and allowed possible crossing during the millennium.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Satan’s influence meant God had lost control?

answers.summary: Arnold said God remained on the throne and in control while permitting Satan’s evil spirit to act. He urged using the authority he associated with Luke 10:19 rather than submitting to that influence.

questions.question: Did Arnold think someone with spiritual understanding could fail to notice an evil influence?

answers.summary: Arnold calls it possible and says people may not recognize what contributes to a fall. This records his spiritual explanation without diagnosing an individual as having an evil spirit.

questions.question: Did Arnold think the antichrist could be a woman?

answers.summary: Arnold said no because he identified the antichrist as Satan himself, whom he described as male. He also rejected identifying that figure as an ordinary person born of a woman.

questions.question: Did Arnold think women knowingly married fallen angels in his Genesis interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold said perhaps not in every case and placed blame and punishment on the fallen angels in his reading of Jude 6. He described hybrid offspring and linked their destruction with the flood. These are his interpretations, not established accounts of human reproduction.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat an unwanted divorce and remarriage as an automatic bar to pastoring?

answers.summary: Arnold said no in the listener’s described circumstances, appealing to forgiveness and Romans 11:29. He qualified his answer with the pastor being genuinely called and repentance for any wrongdoing of his own. This is pastoral interpretation, not a legal ruling.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Dan or Ephraim’s omission as excluding individuals from salvation?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that conclusion, distinguishing national prophetic roles from an individual’s choice and personal salvation. He expressly included people regardless of tribe or race.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat deception by antichrist as an automatic final sentence to the second death?

answers.summary: Arnold said people deceived into worshipping Satan were not automatically doomed to the second death. He emphasized millennium instruction and reserved final judgment for God rather than human declarations.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat eating a rare steak as eating forbidden blood?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished proper bleeding at slaughter from how thoroughly a clean animal’s steak is cooked. He said a rare steak was not the prohibition’s target; this records his religious interpretation rather than food-safety guidance.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Elijah and Enoch as possible two witnesses?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected the listener’s pair from Elijah and Ezekiel to Elijah and Enoch. He called them very likely candidates, preserving that level of uncertainty rather than declaring a settled identification.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat illness as proof someone had offended God?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Job as a counterexample to friends blaming illness on wrongdoing. He said illnesses exist in the world and referred to Satan’s role in Job 1, while urging prayer and obedience. He did not establish the medical cause of the listener’s illness.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat instantly in Ecclesiastes 12 as a printed word or an inference?

answers.summary: Challenged because instantly was absent from the passage, Arnold defended an immediate return of the spirit by reasoning from the silver cord breaking. He described aging and the body returning to dust. His answer offers an interpretation of the timing, not evidence that the English word instantly appears in those verses.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Matthew 24 and Mark 13 as fully fulfilled in AD 70?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that interpretation and centers the chapters on Christ’s return and the fig-tree generation. His answer does not separately analyze every historical layer of the passages.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Peter’s vision as permission to eat any food?

answers.summary: Arnold said no and connected food created to be received in 1 Timothy 4:3 with Leviticus 11. He described scavengers as useful for their created purpose. His dietary and health claims are reported as religious interpretation, not individual nutritional advice.

questions.question: Did Dennis allow someone to split a tithe between two churches?

answers.summary: Dennis said to tithe where taught God’s word and allowed a proportional split when instruction genuinely comes from two churches. His example was an equal split for equal feeding.

questions.question: Did Dennis apply no work, no food to people trying to find work?

answers.summary: Dennis applied 2 Thessalonians 3:10 to people able to work who refuse to do so. He distinguished those trying to find work or temporarily needing help and supported offering them a helping hand.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve a step-grandchild calling someone Grandma?

answers.summary: Dennis said yes and encouraged reciprocal recognition of the child as a granddaughter.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve prepaying utilities for his expected antichrist period?

answers.summary: Dennis approved the listener’s proposal to prepay electricity, water and trash service while setting aside food. His brief answer was preparation advice within his end-time interpretation, without a guarantee about any provider or future event.

questions.question: Did Dennis assign antichrist a particular national region?

answers.summary: Dennis described a claim over the whole world rather than one region and said national identities would not be the basis of that rule.

questions.question: Did Dennis attribute the Egyptian pyramids to aliens?

answers.summary: Dennis explained biblical strangers as human foreigners and did not offer an alien-builder explanation. For further pyramid study he recommended two works in the ministry’s reference library; those authors are not used as independent teaching authorities here.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe another person’s curse could control a Christian?

answers.summary: Dennis denied that power to people using curses or voodoo and urged rejecting evil in Christ’s name. He distinguished human threats from the blessings and curses he associated with God’s covenant.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe deceased people ordinarily watch people on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis said he did not believe they ordinarily could see into this dimension, but allowed that God could permit it for a purpose. He distinguished such an exception from continuous observation.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe God personally walked and talked with Adam and Eve?

answers.summary: Dennis answered yes and compared it with God appearing and speaking to Moses.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe Job lived alongside dinosaurs?

answers.summary: Dennis corrected the listener: he placed Job as a flesh man after the dinosaurs and understood God’s reference to behemoth in Job 40 as looking back to a first earth age. He said that age contained spiritual beings rather than flesh humans. He did not give a date or duration for it.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe Judas was Satan’s son?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected the listener’s suggestion that Judas was Satan’s son. He acknowledged different names or roles attributed to Satan but said that proposed parentage did not follow.

questions.question: Did Dennis clearly say whether returning fallen angels could be distinguished from humans?

answers.summary: Dennis began an answer about distinguishability, then backed up to discuss the absence of hybrids and angelic restraint. The saved response does not clearly complete the specific question about recognizing returning angels.

questions.question: Did Dennis confirm that particular UFO sightings were angels?

answers.summary: Dennis replied that nothing flying is unidentified to God. He did not verify any particular sighting or identify it as an angel.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider it wrong to pray the prayer of Jabez?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is nothing wrong with asking God for blessings and treats Jabez’s prayer as an example. He emphasizes living a life God can bless and both studying and doing what is pleasing to Him.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider playing video games after Bible study wrong?

answers.summary: Dennis said wholesome entertainment can have a place alongside study. He advised moderation, prayer and discipline, especially because the listener had previously struggled to limit play. He also urged parents to monitor games and Internet use. His further suggestion linking violent games with school violence was his opinion, not a finding established by this review.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe the ancestry he called Kenite as spiritual or physical?

answers.summary: Dennis described it as physical and appealed to his reading of Strong’s Hebrew entries and the serpent-seed interpretation. This preserves his teaching without treating it as verified genetics or assigning that ancestry to modern people.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe the end of the world as the end of an age?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguished the end of an age from the disappearance of the earth and described three ages ending in eternity. He connected dinosaur extinction with Satan’s rebellion within that interpretation; this is not a scientific conclusion established here.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish a minister’s pay from preaching for money?

answers.summary: Dennis contrasted serving wealth with a worker receiving support. He allowed payment while saying money should not be the motive for preaching, and advised noticing ministries focused chiefly on financial pressure.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish hunting from animal sacrifice for sins?

answers.summary: Dennis approved hunting and distinguished it from killing an animal as a sacrifice to cover sin. He said the latter had been fulfilled by Christ and noted that biblical hunting provided food; he did not claim Scripture specifically documented sport hunting.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish Moses’ father-in-law Reuel from other men with that name?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jethro is a title meaning his excellency and identifies Reuel as the given name. He says several people in the Bible bear the name Reuel and recommends a Bible dictionary to distinguish them.

questions.question: Did Dennis encourage a nine-year-old to teach or share Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis encouraged beginning to share faith with friends while first learning the word. He recommended following in a personal Bible to learn where its books are located rather than relying only on screen text.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate purgatory with the gulf in paradise?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected purgatory as a human tradition and distinguished it from the two sides of the gulf in his reading of Luke 16.

questions.question: Did Dennis exclude a listener born before 1948 from being useful in God’s plan?

answers.summary: Dennis reassured the listener that her birth year did not settle the issue. He described the elect being present during antichrist’s time and emphasized the importance of the remnant passing truth along as well.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect an elect believer to help a brother during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis said yes and used Ezekiel 44:25 to discuss family access. He also applied a married-sister exception through his understanding of family membership after marriage. That restriction is his interpretation rather than a general rule asserted by this FAQ.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect fallen angels to arrive in vehicles like Ezekiel described?

answers.summary: Dennis said he thought so and described it as a possible vehicle resembling his reading of Ezekiel 1. He qualified both the prediction and its visibility, suggesting a different dimension might prevent seeing it. These are his speculations.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect God to dwell above the earth or on a renewed earth?

answers.summary: Dennis described the new earth as the same earth renewed in a new age. He said God’s throne would come here and associated Jerusalem’s name meaning the Lord is there with that future dwelling.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect God to restore the earth’s original condition?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted Revelation 21’s new heaven and earth as rejuvenation of what God created to be inhabited.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect God’s eternal dwelling to be on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis described eternity on a rejuvenated earth, with evil removed and Jerusalem as God’s chosen place. He appealed to Revelation 21–22 and consuming-fire imagery. The captions name Timothy for another allusion; that uncertain citation is not silently corrected.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect ISIS to take over Jerusalem in this answer?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected that expectation. The listener’s handwritten place name was uncertain to him, and this records his broadcast-era prediction rather than a verified current-events conclusion.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect people in heaven to communicate with one another or with earth?

answers.summary: Dennis expected communication among people in heaven and believed they would share an understandable language. He did not expect ordinary communication with people still on earth, though he allowed that God might permit an exceptional circumstance.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect racial separation in eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis said he did not believe people would be kept separate by race and emphasized belonging to Abraham’s seed in Christ regardless of ethnicity. His captioned Revelation chapter-and-verse number is invalid and is not silently corrected.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect the Chapel to keep teaching through the sixth and seventh trumpets?

answers.summary: Dennis said they would teach as long as able and expected teaching in the millennium after the seventh trumpet, while doubting that it would be through television.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect the cloven tongue to be the language of eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis said he thought so and expected one language in the third earth age. He related the present variety of languages to Babel. His identification of the future language remained an opinion, not a certainty.

questions.question: Did Dennis find Noah’s wife named in Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis said Scripture did not supply the names of Noah’s wife or his three daughters-in-law, although it says they were aboard the ark.

questions.question: Did Dennis find the worldwide web or nuclear plants described in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no to both parts of the listener’s question without further explanation.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a definite date for antichrist’s appearance?

answers.summary: Dennis connected his fig-tree-generation interpretation with 1948 and listed forty-, seventy- and one-hundred-twenty-year generation lengths. He did not give one definite date in this answer. These are dated interpretive claims, not a current countdown or verified forecast.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a double rainbow special biblical significance?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses the rainbow as the sign of God’s covenant in Genesis 9:13–15, without assigning the double rainbow its own special meaning. He contrasts Noah’s flood with what he interprets as Satan’s flood of deception in Revelation 12:15–16.

questions.question: Did Dennis give numbers for how many people of each race God created?

answers.summary: Dennis said the answer was not written in Scripture and emphasized that God called his creation good. He did not supply population figures.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify King James with the New Testament James?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguished King James from the New Testament James and described the later king’s connection with the English translation. The captioned elapsed-time unit is erroneous or unclear and is not used as historical dating here.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Revelation 11’s two witnesses with antichrist and the false prophet?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected that identification and described the witnesses as helping accomplish God’s plan by supplying truth to the elect. He connected them with Zechariah’s anointed ones and the song of Moses. His stated interval after their death is retained in the source for audio checking, not silently recalculated.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the headings in Psalm 119 as months or Hebrew letters?

answers.summary: Dennis identified them as the Hebrew alphabet, with twenty-two sections of eight verses and the verses in each section beginning with the corresponding Hebrew letter in the original language. He called the psalm an acrostic.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the United Nations as the completed one-world political system?

answers.summary: Dennis described the United Nations and European Union as developments in that direction. He pointed to the EU’s common currency and urged watchfulness rather than declaring the final political system fully formed. This summarizes the broadcast’s historical comments, not current political analysis.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret born of water in John 3:5 as mandatory baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted water there as natural birth rather than baptism and contrasted birth through a woman with his fallen-angel teaching. That is his interpretation of the verse; he did not give a complete general baptism explanation in this answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret outer darkness as outer space?

answers.summary: Dennis said it meant being outside God’s kingdom, not outer space. He connected Matthew 22:13 with the virgins lacking oil in Matthew 25 and interpreted the oil as truth.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the aliens in Hebrews 11:34 as extraterrestrials?

answers.summary: Dennis said the armies of aliens meant foreign peoples rather than space creatures. He also referred to God and souls with him in heaven within his teaching about life before and after flesh existence.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the fruit eaten in Eden as literal fruit?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no, connecting the tree of knowledge with the serpent and Eve’s seduction in his interpretation. He noted that Genesis does not name an apple. His explanation is kept separate from Scripture’s actual wording.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the Witch of Endor’s apparition as Samuel or an evil spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis described an evil spirit masquerading as Samuel and warned against attempts to communicate with the dead or familiar spirits. He also referred to the witch’s surprise in 1 Samuel 28:12 without fully explaining his phrase that she got more than she bargained for.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to addressing Father, Son and Holy Spirit individually?

answers.summary: Dennis said the listener’s prayer practice was acceptable if understood within his teaching that Father, Son and Holy Spirit are roles or offices of one heavenly Father rather than three separate entities.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to saying bless you after a sneeze?

answers.summary: Dennis approved the expression as wishing someone good health. He also recalled German greetings; the captioned foreign-language words and their explanations have not been verified.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit using part of a tithe for Bible study reference works?

answers.summary: Dennis said it was acceptable to use part of what would otherwise be tithed for reference works or teaching materials to prepare for serving God. His description of ministry finances is the broadcast’s statement, not a current financial audit.

questions.question: Did Dennis place Satan’s expulsion from heaven after the seventh trumpet?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the listener’s claim that Satan is expelled after the seventh trumpet. He says it happens before that trumpet, when Michael and his angels prevail against Satan and his angels, and directs the listener to Revelation 12:6 and following.

questions.question: Did Dennis place testimony before antichrist in flesh or spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis said the elect would still be in flesh because Christ had not yet returned. He also said both elect and non-elect people would remain in flesh until that return.

questions.question: Did Dennis predict that Satan would accuse the two witnesses of being antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis called that accusation possible, not certain. He said the elect would recognize the witnesses through their role in supplying truth, referring to Zechariah 4.

questions.question: Did Dennis read the ten virgins as proof of a rapture?

answers.summary: Dennis said no. He interpreted the oil as truth, the bridegroom as Christ and the unprepared virgins as people deceived by antichrist. He emphasized preparation before the bridegroom returns.

questions.question: Did Dennis recognize a 72-year biblical generation?

answers.summary: Dennis said no and listed forty, seventy and one hundred twenty years as the generation lengths he recognized. He supplied no supporting references in this short answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend prepaid grocery cards for the antichrist period?

answers.summary: Dennis considered prepayment a possible preparation but warned that, in his scenario, a card might have to be exchanged for one requiring antichrist worship. He stressed refusing that worship and also suggested stored food and silver for barter. These were his speculative preparation suggestions, not assurances about payment systems or investments.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend putting a Bible in anointing oil?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected soaking a Bible as unbiblical. He advised putting a small amount of virgin olive oil in a vial, asking God to bless it for obedient use, keeping it for anointing and anointing in Jesus Christ’s name. He attributed the power to God, not the oil.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard farm-raised catfish as clean food?

answers.summary: Dennis says farming does not make catfish clean under his reading of Leviticus 11:9–10. He explains that aquatic food must have fins and scales, and catfish lack scales.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard private vows as a substitute for a marriage license?

answers.summary: Dennis recommended obtaining a marriage license and emphasized responsibility toward children if a relationship ends. His comments about legal protection are recorded as his advice in the broadcast, not a verified statement of current family law.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard studying with Shepherd’s Chapel on television as attending church?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes, telling the listener that studying with the Chapel is being in church. He appeals to Jesus’ statement about gathering in his name and says the viewers are gathered in that name.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard three seeds placed in Adam’s mouth as biblical?

answers.summary: Dennis answers that the story of three seeds being placed in Adam’s mouth when he died is not biblical.

questions.question: Did Dennis require a separate tongues experience to receive the Holy Spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis said that if Christ is in a person, the Holy Spirit is also present, describing Father, Son and Spirit as inseparable. Suspecting that the listener meant tongues, he contrasted unintelligible speech requiring an interpreter with his reading of the universally understood speech in Acts 2.

questions.question: Did Dennis require flowing water for baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis said a baptismal tank is acceptable. He distinguished the water from cleansing through Christ’s blood, while explaining his preference for the Chapel’s outdoor baptisms at Spavinaw Creek.

questions.question: Did Dennis restrict salvation to God’s elect?

answers.summary: Dennis said salvation is not limited to the elect. He described the elect as relatively few and said a much larger number would receive salvation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Christians should follow the old law or the new covenant?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguished laws, statutes and ordinances rather than discarding everything in the Old Testament. He said prohibitions on murder and stealing still apply, while blood-sacrifice ordinances were fulfilled at the cross. He recommended Arnold’s study on the law.

questions.question: Did Dennis say infant sprinkling without later immersion condemns someone?

answers.summary: Dennis said lack of immersion did not by itself mean condemnation. He nevertheless encouraged a person sprinkled as an infant to choose baptism knowingly, following Christ’s example and its symbolism of death, burial and resurrection.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jesus knows our thoughts?

answers.summary: Dennis answered yes, identifying Jesus and God as one. He appealed to John’s presentation of Christ and Jesus’ statement in John 14 that seeing him is seeing the Father.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jonah’s fish delivered him directly to Nineveh?

answers.summary: Dennis said Jonah 2:10 described the fish depositing Jonah on dry land, not at Nineveh. He distinguished that event from the later command in Jonah 3:1–2 to go to Nineveh.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Lot’s daughter was handed over and killed?

answers.summary: Dennis said Lot offered his daughters but they were not handed over and killed. He distinguished Genesis 19 from the account in Judges of the Levite’s concubine being abused and dying.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Michael was released onto earth before Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected that premise and placed Michael’s battle with Satan in heaven. He said Michael’s side prevails and casts Satan and his angels onto earth.

questions.question: Did Dennis say only the one-third who followed Satan enter flesh life?

answers.summary: Dennis said all souls enter flesh life in his earth-age teaching, with exceptions he named for archangels and fallen angels. He explicitly labeled his further thought about the rebellious third being present in the fig-tree generation an educated guess without documentation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say ordinary people can read minds?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no and said only God can read a person’s mind. He explicitly included Satan among those he said could not do so.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people enter the lake of fire immediately at death?

answers.summary: Dennis said people do not enter that final lake immediately at death and described two sides of paradise from Luke 16. He urged sincere repentance and reassured a believer about final condemnation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people on both sides of the gulf have spirit bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes. He cites 1 Corinthians 15:50 and says flesh and blood cannot enter God’s kingdom, so people on either side of the gulf are in spirit bodies.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people taught the rapture are automatically doomed?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are not doomed to hell simply because they believed in the rapture. He describes the millennium as a time of teaching for those who never had an opportunity to hear what he calls the truth, including people raised with rapture teaching.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Scripture promises forgiveness 490 times per day?

answers.summary: Dennis said the passage does not specifically say per day. He connected Peter’s question about forgiving a brother with seven times seventy and extended the illustration to God forgiving sincere repentance.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed together?

answers.summary: Dennis said both were destroyed at the same time and distinguished dictionary dates from the event’s date. His approximate historical dating was not independently checked.

questions.question: Did Dennis say throwing a Bible makes someone antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis said no. He considered throwing it disrespectful but did not identify that person as antichrist.

questions.question: Did Dennis support donating organs after death?

answers.summary: Dennis called organ donation a gift that could help another person. He said departed people would not need their flesh organs again, while acknowledging that the Bible does not directly discuss modern transplantation.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that all people descend from Noah?

answers.summary: Dennis said no and appealed to his interpretation of the separate creation of peoples in Genesis 1. His further assertions about racial ancestry and biological impossibility are unverified doctrinal claims, not accepted here as genetics or a measure of anyone’s worth.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that descendants of fallen angels were present today?

answers.summary: Dennis said no, describing the flood and the sword of Israel as removing the groups in his interpretation. He referred to the fallen angels being restrained in Jude. These are attributed interpretations, not claims established about any living group.

questions.question: Did Dennis think a soul faithful in his first earth age could later follow Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis answered that it was possible and said teaching the word was intended to prevent deception. This is an answer within his earth-age interpretation, not an independently established account of pre-birth conduct.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Eve knew she was pregnant in his serpent-seed interpretation?

answers.summary: Dennis thought she knew, if not immediately then soon afterward, and appealed to Genesis 3:15–16. This records his serpent-seed interpretation, not verified parentage or genetics.

questions.question: Did Dennis think fallen angels could repent?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no and described Satan and fallen angels as condemned, while also expecting their temporary release and casting to earth. His digression about Paul’s head-covering passage includes an uncertain book reference and is not silently corrected here.

questions.question: Did Dennis think God transformed the Egyptian magicians’ rods?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no. He described the magicians’ acts as illusion or trickery, named them from 2 Timothy 3:8, and used the account as a warning to prepare against deceptive displays. He also distinguished Antichrist as supernatural.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Jesus was crucified on a cross or a stake?

answers.summary: Dennis said he believed it was a Roman cross because the Romans were in authority, while saying the distinction was not central to his answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis think the two witnesses would know their purpose?

answers.summary: Dennis answered yes, adding that God’s elect know their purpose as well.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat pain in old age as punishment for earlier sins?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no and described bodily difficulties as part of aging. He encouraged following a doctor’s instructions rather than assuming pain proves divine punishment. This is a summary of his pastoral answer, not a diagnosis.

questions.question: Did Dennis understand Christ’s white horse literally?

answers.summary: Dennis said he thought the white war horse of Revelation 19 was literal and distinguished Christ from the earlier rider he identified with antichrist in Revelation 6. His Greek-word explanation is preserved as his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Jesus know who his disciples were before he met them?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is certain Jesus knew his disciples before meeting them. He reasons that Jesus called them to follow him rather than first asking their identities.

questions.question: Do I have to go to a particular church to be saved?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray states that churches don't save. Jesus Christ saves, and any church that claims to exclusively offer God's salvation isn't a member of the body of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Do those deceived by the anti-Christ have a chance?

answers.summary: Dennis says there are no second chances, while arguing that many people deceived by false teaching have never had a first opportunity to understand. He describes the millennium as teaching and expresses hope that some can thereby be kept from the lake of fire.

questions.question: Do you know what happened to or where is the cross that Jesus was crucified on?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture does not state what became of the crucifixion cross. He imagines that the wood has long since disappeared, making clear that this is his supposition.

questions.question: Do you think that Arnold is still getting rewards in heaven now for the tapes that you show on TV?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes to the question about Arnold’s continuing rewards. He describes Arnold’s recorded teaching as continuing work on earth and calls it double duty. He then shares his own picture of Arnold accompanying Christ, rather than presenting that picture as a documented promise.

questions.question: Does God hear sinners' prayers?

answers.summary: Arnold Murray states that God hears all prayers, but does not always answer them. He emphasizes trusting in God's will and working at receiving blessings, as God knows what is needed and will provide when you trust and obey Him.

questions.question: Does my dad, who has passed away, know that I am watching you?

answers.summary: Arnold tells the listener that her father knows she is studying the Word. He says her father is with the Father and encourages her to continue the study her father had directed her toward. This source-specific assurance remains attributed to Arnold.

questions.question: Does poverty mean God does not love someone?

answers.summary: Dennis says a person can live in poverty and still be rich in the Lord’s eyes. He cites Smyrna in Revelation 2:9 and explains its riches in terms of possessing what he calls the truth.

questions.question: Does the antichrist come from Africa?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that interpretation. He says Revelation’s lion imagery concerns deception and identifies Revelation 12 as his explanation of Satan being cast from heaven.

questions.question: Does the Holy Spirit in us mean that the intellective God is in us?

answers.summary: Arnold Murray says a form of the intellective God is in us through the Holy Spirit. This intellect is absorbed and can be accessed when reading Scripture, similar to how our spirit is the intellect of our soul, though only about 10% of knowledge is retained in the flesh body.

questions.question: Does the mention of the seven trumps mean we will actually hear the sound of a trumpet when they begin, and if so, will they be sounded one after another or spread out over time?

answers.summary: Dennis explains the trumpets as specific events that must occur before Christ returns, rather than simply audible trumpet blasts. He points to Matthew 24 and Mark 13 and recommends Arnold’s separate study on those chapters.

questions.question: Elaine in Pennsylvania asked about the fate of a bipolar person who denies God after being raised in the church.

answers.summary: Dennis Murray stated that God knows our strengths and handicaps, is compassionate, and loves His children. He emphasized that God is not looking for people to zap, and many churches focus too much on fear rather than teaching His love.

questions.question: Ezekiel 28:18, it seems to say Satan will be brought to ashes. In the sight of all them that behold thee. Is this his fate? To burn, or burn in hell?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the king of Tyrus in Ezekiel 28:18 with Satan. He interprets being reduced to ashes and Revelation 20:14–15 as the final death of the soul, rather than ordinary flesh being burned.

questions.question: For what reason do you think God has humans here for? A special purpose?

answers.summary: Arnold explains: the pastor explained that God has humans here because they are his children and he loves them, and he wants to determine if they will love him or follow Satan, as part of separating souls for the next earth age.

questions.question: Have you seen the movie Noah?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor hasn't seen the movie and can't confirm if it's a lie, but he commends the listener for comparing the movie to Scripture and emphasizes that truth aligns with God's word, while falsehood doesn't align with it and is a lie.

questions.question: Hazel in North Dakota asked for an explanation of Acts 19:5-6, especially regarding speaking in tongues.

answers.summary: Dennis Murray explained that the tongues spoken in Acts 19:5-6 were the same as in Acts 2:3, a language understood by people from all over the world without needing interpretation, reflecting the unique nature of the event in Acts 2:3 and its repetition in Acts 19:5-6.

questions.question: How can I get rid of an American Standard Bible I have? Can I throw it away or would that be a sin?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray states that the Bible does not instruct on destroying a worn-out Bible, and suggests burning or burying it as acceptable methods, similar to disposing of a symbol of freedom like the flag.

questions.question: How can you tell for sure if you're a Cainite? If I really am a Cainite and accepted Jesus Christ as my Lord and Savior in my heart and truly have repented, am I still a Cainite?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray explains that a Cainite is a descendant of Cain, a race of people. Accepting Jesus Christ doesn't change your bloodline, but spiritually, you become a child of the living God.

questions.question: How certain was Arnold about people recognizing someone unseen at death?

answers.summary: Arnold described bedside experiences in which dying people seemed to recognize and speak to someone he could not see. He explicitly said he had not experienced that transition himself and could not say whether the unseen person answered; he offered a possible comforting explanation, not proof.

questions.question: How certain was Arnold about the kind of gopher wood used for the ark?

answers.summary: Arnold says the exact wood is unknown and proposes a resinous wood such as pine or cypress. His uncertainty is retained rather than assigning a definite species.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a family struggling with an adult son’s alcohol addiction?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages prayer and uses the prodigal son as an example of someone recognizing the need to change after hardship. He continues his earlier advice against enabling the behavior. This records his pastoral response, not a clinical treatment plan.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a listener not learning Scripture at her church?

answers.summary: Arnold declined to decide whether she should leave, saying God might have a purpose for her there. He recommended prayer and close reading of 2 John to inform her conscience and decision.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a listener struggling with procrastination?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended the acrostic Psalm just studied and a forthcoming study of Psalm 37. His practical advice was to begin with the hardest task and make steady progress, even one task a day.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a new believer whose bereaved father would not attend church?

answers.summary: Arnold warned that pushing can drive someone away and advised gentle encouragement. He recommended learning his teaching about the dead to offer comfort concerning the father’s deceased mother.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a parent discussing the Big Bang with a child?

answers.summary: Arnold expressed disagreement with the school’s account but urged gentleness rather than driving the child away through total rejection. He suggested giving examples and allowing learning. His cosmological interpretation is not a scientific verification.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a parent who did not want an adult child’s drug-using partner in her home?

answers.summary: Arnold supports the parent’s right to set a boundary in her own home and not admit the partner. He treats that as protecting the household rather than rejecting her daughter.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a student concerned about a friend smoking marijuana?

answers.summary: Arnold urges caution about the friendship and objects to the conduct as unlawful and potentially leading to other drug use. Those are his historical pastoral and legal claims, not a statement of current law or an individual medical assessment.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a wife whose husband exaggerated and lied?

answers.summary: Arnold said he could not tell how serious the reported lying was and did not approve it. He suggested setting a good example, referred to 1 Corinthians 7 and qualified his reassurance with the behavior not involving very serious matters. His answer was based on limited details.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise Bible study for someone at a crossroads?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends choosing a biblical book and reading it chapter by chapter rather than studying in confusion. He mentions prophets but does not prescribe an individual life decision.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise correcting earlier rapture teaching given to children?

answers.summary: Arnold urged the parent to learn the scriptural reasoning well before teaching the children and recommended his Rapture Doctrine, True or False study. He emphasized being able to document the teaching rather than merely asserting a new conclusion.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise distinguishing true teaching from false teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold advises comparing teaching with Scripture and reading in context, including time, audience and subject. He urges listeners to study rather than rely solely on a teacher’s claim.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise finding people who follow the true Christ?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages prayer, sound judgment and meeting with believers while acknowledging good people can be found in many places. He emphasizes discernment rather than a guaranteed venue.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise handling a relative’s rude or vulgar talk in the listener’s home?

answers.summary: Arnold supports setting household boundaries instead of passively tolerating the language. He also encourages living an example and allowing for possible change rather than forcing a discussion.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise honoring a mother who had attempted suicide?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged gratitude for the mother having given the listener life and urged recognizing her illness rather than reducing her to her actions. His suggestion about bodily imbalances was a tentative pastoral explanation, not a diagnosis. The answer did not provide crisis-care instructions.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise introducing newly learned Bible teaching to family?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended planting small seeds, answering follow-up questions and avoiding presenting everything at once. He illustrated this with his America-as-Israel interpretation, but also said to keep loving relatives who did not receive it. His example’s ancestry claim remains his interpretation.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise looking up chief prince in Ezekiel 38?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected the listener’s use of the Greek dictionary and directed her to the Hebrew entry for chief in Ezekiel 38:2. The subsequent name and historical-language wording is damaged in the captions and is not reconstructed here.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise preparing to answer other people’s questions?

answers.summary: Arnold urged knowing the subject, preparation and discernment, while being willing to say I do not know and research the answer. He encouraged sharing what one did understand and learning together rather than pretending to know everything.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise preparing to stand against Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends prayer, studying Scripture and putting on the spiritual armor described in Ephesians 6. He describes the struggle as spiritual rather than against flesh.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise responding to favoritism within a Christian family?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly advised forgiveness and responding as a bigger Christian. He did not investigate the family’s circumstances or give a detailed plan.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise responding to Happy Easter greetings?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended discernment and gently sharing a small point with someone receptive, following up if they asked more. He warned against trying to correct whole churches and said only God could make the seed grow.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise responding to persecution?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages prayer, wise avoidance of persecutors where possible and being wise as a serpent and gentle as a dove. He does not give a definite reason why some face more persecution than others.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise responding to someone announcing false Christ?

answers.summary: Arnold advised not letting the person control the conversation, using a brief response and moving on. His agree-or-disagree illustration reverses its wording in the captions, so that disputed wording remains held instead of being turned into a command.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone meeting an atheist family member?

answers.summary: Arnold advised demonstrating Christian character and genuine care rather than expecting Scripture alone to persuade someone who rejects it. He offered 1 Corinthians 10:13 for the listener’s own encouragement.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone observing Passover without a local church?

answers.summary: Arnold said the listener could participate with the televised service or partake knowing Christ was present. He referred to Christ as Passover in 1 Corinthians 5:7–8, not a requirement to join a particular local church.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone repeatedly committing the same sin?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages honest prayer for strength to stop, rather than asking forgiveness without addressing the repeated conduct. He warns that an unaddressed weakness can become a means of deception.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone struggling to understand Revelation?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged studying Revelation with guided teaching rather than abandoning it for another book. He noted Daniel’s relationship to Revelation, but said a teacher could help the listener understand the revealing itself.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone wanting God in her life?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages sincere repentance, accepting forgiveness and forgiving oneself. He reassures the listener of God’s love and continuing presence.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone who did not know how to pray?

answers.summary: Arnold describes prayer as honest conversation with the Father, aloud or silently. He emphasizes trust that God hears and recommends asking according to God’s will, while acknowledging that the answer may differ from what the person wants.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone who felt unsure of her faith?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages belief in Jesus as God’s Son, studying Scripture and speaking to God from the heart. He reassures the listener that no one remembers every passage and that Scripture remains available to consult.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone who had made a vow to God?

answers.summary: Arnold says a promise to God should be kept. He distinguishes that from imitating Old Testament vows without understanding the duties he believes God gives believers today.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise speaking with a sister who had been involved in the occult?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended gentle conversation, planting a seed and showing a happy example rather than overwhelming the sister. He suggested Mark 13 and referred to possible help in the millennium through his Ezekiel 44 interpretation. He did not independently verify the reported spirits.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise women facing degrading name-calling?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects abusive name-calling and encourages strength and self-respect. He cites women such as Deborah and recommends his Women of the Bible study; the answer does not provide a specific safety plan.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a bereaved listener who also asked about his Marine service?

answers.summary: Arnold comforts the listener by saying his mother is with the Father and that they will be reunited. He also expresses gratitude for serving in the Marine Corps and discusses his opposition to communism and socialism.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a bereaved parent asking about a child’s short life?

answers.summary: Arnold read Ecclesiastes 9 as referring to the dead flesh body and Ecclesiastes 12:6–7 as the person returning to God. He offered his personal belief that some people were too good for this world. That consolation is not verified knowledge of why the daughter died.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking about dragons being against God?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted the grandmother’s dragon as a name for Satan rather than a fire-breathing creature. His captioned Revelation 9:6–7 reference is questionable and is not silently replaced with a different passage.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking about Xmas?

answers.summary: Arnold explained the Greek chi-rho symbol as referring to Christ, while preferring the full name Christmas so Christ was not left out. He also repeated his interpretation of Christmas as marking conception. These are his explanation and preference.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking how to please God?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged the teenager to continue what she was doing after she described studying and asked her questions. He did not give an additional list of requirements.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking when God would come and Satan would die?

answers.summary: Arnold said only the Father knows the date, then described his five-month interpretation and a captioned three-day interval after the witnesses’ deaths. He did not finish a separate explanation of Satan’s final death. The interval is preserved as stated here rather than harmonized with other answers.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking whether animals can be angels?

answers.summary: Arnold spoke of animals having spiritual form and being present in God’s future order, referring to Isaiah 11. The captions initially say angels before clarifying animals, so this answer does not establish that animals are heavenly messengers.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking whether God is angry when people do not study?

answers.summary: Arnold said God is pleased when people study and recognized differing appetites for study. He added that neglecting God’s word entirely displeases God.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking who God’s father is?

answers.summary: Arnold appealed to God’s declaration I am that I am and said God is what he wishes to be. He did not identify a parent for God, instead saying fuller understanding would come later.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking why God made earth?

answers.summary: Arnold described earth as a place prepared for God’s children and referred to Job 38. He added his firmament-canopy and future-restoration account; those physical claims are his interpretation rather than independently verified science.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child worried that moving would mean abandoning a church ministry?

answers.summary: Arnold said he did not know the family’s circumstances or whether another calling was involved. He suggested that pastors remain able to minister after moving rather than assuming their calling ends.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a disagreement between Strong’s and Green’s Interlinear?

answers.summary: Arnold preferred Strong’s for the listener’s translation question while still recommending Green’s as an inexpensive way to consult the underlying texts. He criticized aspects of Green’s translation but the captioned Thessalonians reference and Greek word are damaged. His preference is recorded without independently resolving the disputed entries.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a family considering bankruptcy after an injury?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished unavoidable hardship after injury from using bankruptcy simply to evade debts. He said it may be the remaining option when no other way exists and urged prayerful consideration. This is historical pastoral advice, not a legal or financial assessment of a present case.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a household worried about disability support during the antichrist period?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends keeping a reasonably stocked pantry and reassures the household to care for themselves and trust God. He does not give a prediction about whether their disability payments will continue.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener about Eve’s wording of the garden command?

answers.summary: Arnold affirmed the concern in a limited sense and emphasized the exception in Genesis 2:17. He then gave his symbolic identification of the tree of knowledge with the serpent and the tree of life with Christ. The pronouns are rough in the captions and are not used to invent a new accusation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener afraid that quitting a job had spoiled God’s plan?

answers.summary: Arnold said he could not assess the decision without knowing why she left. He distinguished mistreatment from simply not wanting to work and counseled keeping a needed job until a better opportunity was available.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener asking about a fig tree on the studio set?

answers.summary: Arnold responded humorously about spare fig leaves and said the visible plant was not the fig tree the listener assumed. The plant names in this caption export are uncertain and are not confidently identified here.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener asking about Rahab’s identity?

answers.summary: Arnold argued that Rahab was a businesswoman working with flax rather than a prostitute, then referred to his Ruth study for genealogy. This is his interpretation; his historical and lexical assertions were not independently verified.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener asking how to know they are saved?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured the teenager on the basis of her belief, saying her questions showed it. He did not present a separate ritual or checklist in this brief answer.

Arnold emphasized belief and John 3:16, then explained everlasting life through his first-earth-age teaching. He said no created soul had yet ceased existing and qualified his objection to the word preexistence. This records his doctrinal explanation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener describing severe depression and suicidal thoughts?

answers.summary: Arnold responded forcefully with encouragement about God’s love, purpose and power over enemies, and referred to 1 Corinthians 10:13. He did not discuss clinical assessment or crisis care in this answer. This historical pastoral response is not adequate stand-alone guidance for someone at immediate risk; the Luke chapter recalled in the captions is uncertain.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener distinguishing one human race from ethnicities?

answers.summary: Arnold maintained his use of different races and connected it with his sixth-day creation teaching, while explicitly saying all people were human, had souls and should receive dignity and respect. These are his terminology and creation claims, not a scientific taxonomy of humanity.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener unsure about changing religious groups?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged the listener if she was learning through chapter-and-verse study. He said God may place someone in a particular setting for a reason and declined to decide that an unnamed former group was necessarily the wrong place for her.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener unsure whether antichrist teaching concerned history or the future?

answers.summary: Arnold declined to judge the listener’s former church but identified antichrist as Satan, the son of perdition claiming to be God. He cited 2 Thessalonians 2:2–4, especially verse 4, and Ezekiel 28:18–19. The listener’s earlier-teaching question was unclear; this records the identification he actually gave.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener who had prayed but remained ill?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended anointing and continued prayer for God’s will, saying healing depended on God’s timing. He did not identify a specific sin causing the listener’s illness. This is pastoral advice and does not establish a medical cause or replace clinical care.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener who skips long lists of names?

answers.summary: Arnold allows for differing interests and duties and says the lists often provide chronology. He does not condemn the listener for finding those passages difficult or boring.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener wishing to go back and change the past?

answers.summary: Arnold frames the concern as difficulty forgiving oneself and uses Paul as an example of remorse. He emphasizes sincere repentance and forgiveness rather than promising time travel or a chance to redo events.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener worried about the dollar’s future value?

answers.summary: Arnold expected the dollar to retain value until the monetary change he associated with false Christ and a world system. He also discussed retirement accounts recovering in the circumstances of that broadcast. These are dated comments and predictions, not current financial guidance.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener worried that other nations were taking Israel’s blessings?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted the concern within his end-time and national-identity teaching but said blessings come from God and cannot be taken away by Satan. The listener’s broad claim about other peoples is not independently established.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener’s comparison of deception across three periods?

answers.summary: Arnold agrees with the listener’s comparison of deception in a former age, the antichrist period and the final test after the millennium. He cites Revelation 12 for the one-third imagery. The comparison is his interpretation and is not treated as an independently established account of who experiences each event.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener’s proposed thousand-year interval from Daniel to Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected the proposed thousand-year interval and recommended Appendix 50 of the Companion Bible. His brief spoken dating is unclear in the captions and is not used here to establish a historical chronology.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener’s questions about angels, gender and marriage?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished his proposed third earth age from the present age and said angels in the latter could have gender. He connected fallen angels with his Genesis seduction interpretation and treated resurrection marriage language separately. These are his doctrinal claims, not established accounts of human reproduction.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a low-income listener pressured to send a preacher money?

answers.summary: Arnold told the listener to discard the letter demanding a two-hundred-dollar obedient gift. He rejected its claim to speak for God and distinguished support for teaching from begging or coercion. This is his response to the reported letter, not an independently investigated accusation against a named ministry.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a parent worried her Marine son might fight Israel?

answers.summary: Arnold asserted that it would not happen and recommended Psalm 144, especially its first verse. His assurance was a personal prediction in the broadcast, not a guarantee about future military orders or legal advice to a service member.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a publisher question about the translation captioned Moffett?

answers.summary: Arnold accepted the publisher the listener had found and praised the translation. The captions distort both names, so no exact edition or publisher spelling is asserted as verified and no present availability is claimed.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about a Feast of Tabernacles gathering?

answers.summary: Arnold announced television communion and two in-person services, with reservations and no meal provision. These were plans for that historical broadcast period, not a current event schedule.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about being saved through childbirth?

answers.summary: Arnold praises witnessing childbirth as potentially moving a person toward faith. He does not provide a full interpretation of the biblical phrase or claim that giving birth automatically confers salvation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about British royalty and Judah?

answers.summary: Arnold connects British and Russian royal families with Judah in his interpretation of ancestry and migration. The caption passage contains uncertain names and historical assertions; this is an attributed account of his answer, not verified genealogy or history.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about calling no man father in Matthew 23:9?

answers.summary: Arnold declined to criticize the denomination named in the letter. He urged the listener to understand and follow the Scripture, acknowledging imperfections in all denominations, but did not give a detailed interpretation of the title in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about Jesus’ age and calendar dates?

answers.summary: Arnold maintained an age of thirty-three and suggested a birth date closer to 2 BC than 4 BC. He did not fully reconcile the listener’s calendar calculation in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about keeping Sabbath from midnight to midnight?

answers.summary: Arnold questioned the listener’s account of the other church, said the traditional boundary was sundown rather than midnight and recommended Colossians 2. He affirmed daily rest in Christ. He did not verify that denomination’s actual practice.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about laboratory cloning?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected reports of laboratory cloning and described identical twins as natural clones made by God. He also said God owns all souls. His scientific and historical assertions in this answer are unverified; they are preserved as his statements, not adopted as scientific findings.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about losing constitutional freedom of worship?

answers.summary: Arnold strongly expresses confidence in defending freedom of worship and refers to military service and broadcasting. This is his historical conviction rather than a present legal guarantee or a supplied prophecy of future rights.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about man not living alone?

answers.summary: Arnold first suggests the listener may mean not living by bread alone, citing Luke 4:4 and Deuteronomy 8:3. He also acknowledges Adam receiving Eve as a companion. The answer keeps both possibilities rather than selecting an unstated intended question.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about observing the Feast of Tabernacles today?

answers.summary: Arnold calls the ministry’s observance a fall fellowship and describes it as the start of the civil year on God’s calendar. The brief answer does not provide a full set of observance instructions.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about Palestine and Syria’s tribal origins?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly associated them with Ishmael without supplying evidence or addressing the question’s full political premise. This broad ancestry claim is not independently established and should not be used to classify present individuals.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about requests for money for homeless children?

answers.summary: With time running out, Arnold directs the listener to 2 John. He does not develop an answer that would establish a general rule for charitable giving in this passage.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about the prince’s portion in the Companion Bible plan?

answers.summary: Arnold mentions the Savior as prince and also David as prince of Israel. The captioned question about the plan, area and occupants is damaged, so the answer does not establish a clear allocation of that portion.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about the Shroud of Turin?

answers.summary: Arnold considers the proposed identification with Jesus’ burial cloth possible and discusses the image in response to the listener. His assertion about whether it had been disproved is not a verified assessment of the evidence or a current scientific finding.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about the size of paradise’s gulf?

answers.summary: Arnold describes it as a boundary no one may cross by God’s order, not a distance measured in the answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about Truman, MacArthur and the Chosin Reservoir?

answers.summary: Arnold expresses respect for both men while saying MacArthur received poor field intelligence. He credits General Smith and supporting forces with protecting supply lines and helping troops survive. This is his recollection and assessment, not an independently checked military history.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about whom God addressed in Genesis 3:22?

answers.summary: Arnold described God as speaking to Adam about expulsion from the garden and interpreted the tree of life as Christ. He related access to that tree to Christ’s crucifixion; this preserves his response without substituting a different explanation of the verse.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about wishing on stars and lucky pennies?

answers.summary: Arnold responded lightly to the penny superstition, then redirected the listener toward prayer, loving God and trusting his guidance rather than relying on luck. He did not give a direct blanket prohibition on wishes.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question comparing biblical and present calendars?

answers.summary: Arnold discusses BC and AD and favors solar reckoning. His brief account does not establish that ancient and current calendars are identical in all details.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question comparing pearly gates with the great gulf?

answers.summary: Arnold discussed the book of life, Christ’s judgment seat and the rich man and Lazarus in Luke 16. He said earthly church records were not the authoritative heavenly record. He did not directly locate a passage describing pearly gates in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request about not wishing bad on false teachers?

answers.summary: Arnold says he cannot recall the requested prohibition and directs the listener to Ezekiel 13’s judgment of false teachers. This records his response without turning it into permission to mistreat anyone.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request for a decree or sign about prayer?

answers.summary: Arnold assumes the listener means a fleece, compares it with Gideon and recommends praying, trying, correcting failures and recognizing when a different course is needed. He advises God’s will rather than a guaranteed prayer formula.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request for studying other religions?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends concentrating on Scripture and suggests a general encyclopedia for comparative information. He does not identify or review a particular other religion in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request to broadcast the ministry documentaries for home recording?
