answers.summary: Arnold tentatively recalled a date around the twentieth or twenty-second and said he would keep listeners informed. This is an uncertain historical announcement, not a current schedule.

questions.question: What did Arnold advise someone wanting to reach unbelieving family members?

answers.summary: Arnold began with setting an example and then stressed preserving the opportunity to teach children God’s word. His answer linked this advice to the listener’s accompanying question about 1 Corinthians 7.

questions.question: What did Arnold call the four hidden dynasties?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies political, financial, educational and religious power as the four dynasties in his interpretation of Zechariah 1:18–19. He connects these with Satan’s deception. This is his prophetic interpretation rather than proof of a real-world conspiracy.

questions.question: What did Arnold call the world that was?

answers.summary: Arnold calls it the first world age and points to 2 Peter 3 for his account of three ages.

questions.question: What did Arnold consider appropriate clothing for baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold puts understanding and belief above the clothing, says a bathing suit does not offend him and recommends judgment about modesty and credibility. His baptism anecdote is not a medical safety guarantee.

questions.question: What did Arnold emphasize in God’s description as a green fir tree?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized evergreen as a symbol of enduring life rather than identifying a particular modern species such as Douglas fir. He related the image to eternal life.

questions.question: What did Arnold identify as the light in Genesis 1?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies it with God’s presence and the Holy Spirit rather than Wisdom itself. His firmament and linguistic explanations remain interpretations rather than established physical descriptions.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by a church letter?

answers.summary: Arnold described a church letter as a denominational membership record transferred when a member moves. He distinguished that record from judgment and rewards recorded in heaven’s book of life.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by heaven being closed during the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished those already in the first resurrection from those who must await the second. He said the latter would not complete their overcoming during the millennium until Satan’s release supplied the final test.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by killing the flesh?

answers.summary: Arnold explicitly treated the phrase spiritually: resisting fleshly appetites and following the inward spiritual person. He used Christ’s temptation as an example and referred to two bodies in 1 Corinthians 15. He was not instructing bodily injury. A conflicting flesh-return clause in the captions remains held.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by our people in this answer?

answers.summary: Asked about our people and the oil of our people, Arnold answered believers everywhere. This explicit definition is preserved with its own source.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by rightly dividing Scripture?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized who, what, when and where, using Job 38 to distinguish God’s assessment from the earlier advisers’ speeches. He called the four-question method an oversimplification rather than a complete rule for interpretation.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by studying the Bible in context?

answers.summary: Arnold says to identify who is being addressed, what a passage refers to and its subject. He connects those questions with rightly dividing Scripture.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by teaching on three levels?

answers.summary: Arnold connected three audiences with Paul’s commission in Acts 9:15: Israel, Gentiles and rulers. He urged identifying audience, subject and time when interpreting a passage.

questions.question: What did Arnold recommend as the best way to honor God?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized loving God, connecting Hosea 6:6 with mercy and love and Revelation 4’s final verse with God’s pleasure. This is his explanation of worship and purpose.

questions.question: What did Arnold say a letter marker beside firmament indicated?

answers.summary: Arnold said the attached page’s T marker pointed to a footnote giving expanse as another meaning. The page itself is not available in the captions, so the answer is not generalized to every Bible edition.

questions.question: What did Arnold say about predictions concerning December 2012?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects the proposed planetary alignment and end-of-world certainty, then discusses a claimed alignment involving the solstice and galactic equator. These are historical statements from before December 2012; the astronomical explanation is not independently verified here.

questions.question: What did Arnold say about progress on a proposed Shepherd’s Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold says much work was in the computer but time and training were still needed. This historical progress report does not establish whether a publication was later completed.

questions.question: What did Arnold say about Shepherd’s Chapel operating between the sixth and seventh trumpets?

answers.summary: Arnold expresses hope that the ministry will still be present but says the central event is the elect’s testimony through the Holy Spirit. He predicts the trials will be broadcast around the world; this remains his expectation, not a verified future event.

questions.question: What did Arnold say about the listener’s Light of the World Bible edition?

answers.summary: Arnold describes the edition from the World Publishing Company as a good publication. He also identifies the Bible being discussed as a standard King James Bible in the transition to the next question.

questions.question: What did Arnold say about the location and meaning of the Bat Creek stone?

answers.summary: In this recording Arnold says the stone is held by the Smithsonian and claims to have translated its inscription as a religious message about returning to the Father. Neither its present location nor his proposed translation is independently established by this FAQ.

questions.question: What did Arnold say an economic stimulus should fund?

answers.summary: In this historical broadcast Arnold favors domestic oil production and nuclear power as uses for stimulus spending. These are his political and economic opinions from that broadcast, not a current assessment.

questions.question: What did Arnold say happened to the flesh bodies of those taken by God?

answers.summary: Arnold describes their bodies as transfigured or taken and connects the discussion with the mount of transfiguration. The caption renders one biblical name unclearly.

questions.question: What did Arnold say happens to flesh bodies when Christ returns?

answers.summary: Arnold explained the change in terms of a different dimension and said flesh and blood cannot enter the kingdom. He deferred the requested details about the bodies to his coming study of Zechariah 14, so this occurrence remains an incomplete explanation.

For a second listener asking about flesh bodies at Christ’s return, Arnold said apparently they would return to dust, then again deferred a fuller explanation to Zechariah 14. He repeated his description of a different dimension.

questions.question: What did Arnold say soldiers most wanted from home?

answers.summary: Drawing on his wartime experience, Arnold emphasized love from home. He mentioned homemade cookies as welcome but said a mother’s love mattered more. This was personal encouragement to a parent of a deployed service member.

questions.question: What did Arnold suggest made deception possible in a first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold compares it with present gullibility, impatience and attraction to impressive claims. His long discussion of practical skills illustrates common sense rather than documenting a specific earlier offer by Satan.

questions.question: What did Dennis associate with the number ten?

answers.summary: Dennis associated ten with responsibility and the measurement of judgment and reward. He applied it to responsible witness during the trial described in Revelation 2:10. The listener’s follow-up wording is damaged.

questions.question: What did Dennis call intercourse with another partner while already married?

answers.summary: Dennis qualifies the listener’s statement about intercourse and marriage by referring to the Old Testament expression of spreading a skirt over a woman. He calls intercourse with another person while married to someone else adultery.

questions.question: What did Dennis claim about one parent passing on the ancestry he called Kenite?

answers.summary: Dennis said one parent could pass on that ancestry in his serpent-seed interpretation. This is a doctrinal claim in the broadcast, not a verified genetic classification or a basis for identifying any living person’s ancestry.

questions.question: What did Dennis mean by a shadow government?

answers.summary: Dennis defined it as a supposed arrangement in which private actors exercise power behind elected officials. He offered Absalom’s activity in 2 Samuel 15 as an upcoming biblical illustration rather than proving any modern conspiracy.

questions.question: What did Dennis mean by Strong’s Exhaustive Concordance?

answers.summary: Dennis identified that as the concordance offered through the Chapel and emphasized obtaining what he regarded as Strong’s original definitions. His broader allegation that some publishers alter definitions was not demonstrated or independently verified in this answer.

questions.question: What did Dennis recommend about the Companion Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis described its KJV text, wide-margin notes, outlines, figures of speech and 198 appendices. He credited E. W. Bullinger and said the pastors sometimes paraphrased those notes when explaining a verse.

questions.question: What did Dennis recommend to someone repeatedly troubled by memories of past sins?

answers.summary: Dennis suggested that the listener might not have forgiven herself despite having repented. He encouraged self-forgiveness and recommended Arnold’s Forgiveness study. This is pastoral counsel, not a diagnosis of persistent or intrusive thoughts.

questions.question: What did Dennis say about Isaiah’s ancestry?

answers.summary: Dennis reported a tradition connecting Isaiah’s father with Judah’s royal family and expressly distinguished it from biblical documentation. The tradition was not independently verified here.

questions.question: What did Dennis say about names after entering spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis pointed to a new name in Revelation 3:12 and the name he pronounced from Isaiah 62:4, explaining its meaning as God’s delight in his people. He did not give a general rule that everyone retains an earthly name.

questions.question: What did Dennis say distinguished Philadelphia and Smyrna?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Revelation 3:7 and 2:8–9 and says Philadelphia and Smyrna were the two churches Christ did not fault. He says both taught about those claiming to be Jews while lying, whom he identifies in this answer as Kenites.

questions.question: What did Dennis say Revelation 1:13 describes?

answers.summary: Dennis said Revelation 1:13–20 concerns Jesus Christ and describes his appearance in his transfigured body.

questions.question: What did Jesus preach when he was here on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray says to read Matthew chapters five, six, and seven for the sermon on the Mount, and the other gospels and New Testament writings for what Christ talked about. He mentions Mark chapter 13 where Christ said, 'Behold, I have told you all things.'

questions.question: What divine name did Arnold give for God as provider?

answers.summary: Arnold gives Jehovah Jireh in response to a question about praying for a financial blessing and explains it as God providing. He does not promise a particular financial outcome.

questions.question: What does 2 Thessalonians 2:6 and 7 mean about the ministry of the Holy Spirit hindering the work of the man of sin?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the proposed interpretation that the church’s removal is the restraint in 2 Thessalonians 2:6–7. He identifies Michael as holding Satan back and interprets the eventual release as Michael casting Satan to earth, not the church being raptured.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 9:28 mean to you?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray explains that Hebrews 9:28 refers to the Second Coming of Jesus Christ, where He will appear to those who are looking for Him. He warns that many will be deceived into thinking He has already come when the antichrist appears, but he expresses confidence that Cynthia, who loves studying the word, will not be among them.

questions.question: What does it mean that the hairs of our head are numbered?

answers.summary: Arnold explains it as God’s protection and power over Satan, referring to Luke 21:18.

questions.question: What does it mean to be unequally yoked?

answers.summary: In this answer Arnold explains it as an agreement or partnership that prevents a person from studying God’s Word or exercising faith. He contrasts that burden with taking Christ’s yoke.

questions.question: What does the brass plaque say that is on the pulpit?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray stated he doesn't have a clue what the caller is talking about, explaining there's no plaque on their pulpit and they use hotel-provided lecterns which may have promotional material on them.

questions.question: What does the Song of Solomon mean?

answers.summary: Arnold explains: dr. Murray explains that the Song of Solomon is a love story between Jesus and his bride, focusing on those who love and obey Him. It's a beautiful song that requires study and understanding of its context and characters to fully appreciate its meaning.

questions.question: What does unnatural affection mean?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: it means without natural affection. It means being hard-hearted toward your own family, even.

questions.question: What event did Arnold place three and a half days before Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Revelation 11 and the killing of the two witnesses. He says their deaths precede Christ’s return by three and a half days. The listener’s introductory chronology is not independently adopted as a claim.

questions.question: What evidence did Arnold give for living in the last generation?

answers.summary: Arnold links the fig-tree parable and Jeremiah 24 with Israel becoming a nation in 1948. He leaves the length of the generation to God. The captions render some Psalm references and numbers uncertainly; they are not corrected here.

questions.question: What exactly does the blood and the body of Christ represent?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray explains that the bread represents the body of Christ and the wine represents the blood of Christ, as described in 1 Corinthians 11:23-25.

questions.question: What happened to Mary after Jesus died on the cross?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus entrusted Mary’s care to John. He then expressly distinguishes a nonbiblical historical claim that Mary went with Joseph of Arimathea to Britain and recommends a book about it. That later claim is not presented as Scripture or independently verified history.

questions.question: What happens if a saved person sins without repenting?

answers.summary: Dennis challenges the claim that a saved person remains safe while sinning without repentance. He says people are judged on their works and separately points to the unforgivable sin in Luke 12:10–13 as excluding salvation. The answer does not equate every unrepented sin with that specific sin.

questions.question: What is an elect? And how do you become one?

answers.summary: Dennis says one cannot newly become one of the elect at the time of this recording. He describes them as souls who stood with God in the first age and have a special witness against the antichrist in this age. He connects their overcoming with the first resurrection in Revelation 20:4–6.

questions.question: What is the best book to start studying the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray suggests starting with the book of Genesis, as understanding the beginning of God's word is essential, and also recommends studying the book of Revelation to grasp the end of God's word.

questions.question: What is the definition of an epistle?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: it means a letter. For example, if you turn to your Bible and you go to 1 Corinthians, in the title you'll find, 'The first epistle,' which means letter.

questions.question: What is the true meaning of Luke 17:34?

answers.summary: Arnold explains: the pastor explains that Luke 17:34 refers to the antichrist coming at the sixth trump and the false Christ taking the first one in the field. He encourages readers to follow the subject and not be misled by others.

questions.question: What is your educated opinion of what Jesus was writing when he kneeled and scratched in the sand when the woman was about to be stoned for adultery?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly offers an educated guess that Jesus’ writing exposed the accusers’ own adultery. His examples of particular men and incidents are illustrative speculation. He then recounts the accusers leaving and Jesus telling the woman to sin no more.

questions.question: What language connection did Arnold claim between Arabian and locust?

answers.summary: Arnold tells the listener to compare terms in Strong’s Concordance and claims they are the same word. He then applies locust imagery geographically. The linguistic and ethnic association is not independently verified or adopted as a characterization of a present-day people.

questions.question: What location did Arnold associate with not one stone remaining on another?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the warning with the Jerusalem buildings under discussion, not Rome. He connects the location with his interpretation of Ezekiel 16 and God’s future dwelling.

questions.question: What material did Arnold recommend for studying the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends his Three Earth Ages recording and Companion Bible appendix 146. Current availability is not checked.

questions.question: What meaning did Arnold assign to the number fifteen?

answers.summary: Arnold associated fifteen with rest, citing the fifteenth-day dates he gave for Passover and Tabernacles and connecting rest with Christ as Sabbath.

questions.question: What meaning did Dennis give the name Caiaphas?

answers.summary: Dennis attributed the meaning depression to Smith’s Bible Dictionary and said Caiaphas was appointed high priest by the Romans rather than by God. This preserves his account without independently verifying the dictionary or historical claims.

questions.question: What meanings did Arnold give the number two?

answers.summary: Arnold associated two with a confirming witness, union and possible division. He said it had more than one meaning rather than assigning one fixed meaning in every passage.

questions.question: What next step did Arnold recommend after gaining new understanding?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages retaining Mark 13’s instruction about Spirit-led testimony before the false messiah. He thanks the listener for the testimony but does not assign a specific individual timetable.

questions.question: What opinion did Dennis express about Social Security and Medicare funding in this recording?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes the funding problem he describes to officials spending money for other purposes and says future funding remains uncertain. This is his opinion in the recording, not a verified present-day benefits or funding report.

questions.question: What position did Dennis take on ordaining openly gay clergy?

answers.summary: Dennis opposed it on his interpretation of Leviticus 18:22, Leviticus 20:13 and Romans 1:23–28. He presented this as his reading of Scripture rather than offering an unrelated personal policy opinion.

questions.question: What race are the Cainites?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets Cainites as descendants of Cain and links that identification with John 8:44. He also says they can become children of God by accepting Christ. This is his source-specific teaching, not an identification of any present-day ethnic or religious group.

questions.question: What role did Arnold give overcoming free-will believers in the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly says they will teach along with the elect. He gives no detailed assignment or individual identification.

questions.question: What Scripture did Arnold offer a family whose relative was in a coma?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages prayer and points to 1 Corinthians 10:13 for strength and a way through the trial. The answer offers pastoral comfort; it does not assess the relative’s medical prognosis.

questions.question: What should I do about my 17-year-old son who is badmouthing me?

answers.summary: Dennis advises the mother to have a direct conversation with her son, set clear household boundaries and follow through on consequences. He emphasizes consistency rather than making threats that are not enforced, referring to Hebrews 12:6–7 in his discussion of discipline.

questions.question: What significance did Arnold give the Dome of the Rock?

answers.summary: Arnold associated it with the Temple Mount and described the place as sacred to more than one religion. Some of his comments about other religions and resurrection are imprecise, so they are not repeated as verified history or current control information.

questions.question: What tribe did Dennis assign to Elijah?

answers.summary: Dennis said a tribe was not supplied and identified the recorded description as a Tishbite of Gilead.

questions.question: What view did Arnold express about a Supreme Court gun-ownership case?

answers.summary: Arnold welcomed the court taking the case and hoped it would uphold the right to bear arms. His recollection of the particular case was tentative, and these are historical political comments rather than a statement of current law.

questions.question: What view did Arnold express when asked about global warming?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected global warming and criticized carbon taxation in this historical broadcast. These are his comments, not a verified scientific assessment; the Genesis verse number in the captions is uncertain.

questions.question: When did Arnold expect the one-world system to become fully effective?

answers.summary: Arnold expected an almost-established system to suffer a deadly wound, followed by Satan appearing and healing it. He said it becomes effective after false Christ appears. This is his prophetic interpretation, not a verified current event.

questions.question: When did Arnold place the battle of Ezekiel 38–39?

answers.summary: Arnold places it near the end of this earth age and says God fights the battle without another army intervening.

questions.question: When did Arnold place the marriage supper?

answers.summary: Arnold places it at Christ’s return and the beginning of the millennium.

questions.question: When did Arnold place the time of Jacob’s trouble?

answers.summary: Arnold places it at the end when the antichrist is present and connects it with believers testifying against him. The short answer does not supply a separate Scripture reference.

questions.question: When did Arnold say biblical evening begins?

answers.summary: Arnold answers sundown in response to the question about taking Christ down from the cross.

questions.question: When did Arnold think a pastor could exclude someone from a congregation?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes protecting a congregation from a disruptive or exploitative person from exclusion based only on dislike. He says the pastor must weigh the harm, the person’s need for help and accountability to God.

questions.question: When did Arnold think the 144,000 would receive their sealing?

answers.summary: Arnold said most likely during the tribulation, after hearing the Holy Spirit’s testimony through the elect. He connected Revelation 7 with his reading of Ezekiel 44’s priests going astray. His tentative timing and doctrinal interpretation are retained.

questions.question: When do you think the end of time will be?

answers.summary: Arnold declines to give a calendar date. He points to the fig-tree generation and events described in Mark 13 as signs to watch. He clarifies that he means the end of this dispensation, not the extinction of time or human existence.

questions.question: When the Holy Spirit comes through us, do we speak a language not understandable by others?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the language spoken when the Holy Spirit speaks through us is understood by everyone, regardless of their language. This is evidenced by Acts 2:4-6, where the Holy Spirit spoke in multiple languages, not an unknown tongue requiring interpretation. If someone needs to interpret, it wasn't the Holy Spirit speaking.

questions.question: When you die, do you have any memory of your spiritual body?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks memory is retained. He reasons that fair judgment requires awareness of the actions being judged and urges repentance. His opening qualification is retained rather than converting the answer into certainty.

questions.question: Where can I find the scripture that says when you die your body returns to the ground and your soul goes to heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray says this is in 2 Corinthians, chapter five, verses seven and eight, which was just covered.

questions.question: Where can I find to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray says this is found in 2 Corinthians, the teachings of Paul, chapter five, verses seven and eight, explaining that when we die, our spirit is present with the Lord.

questions.question: Where did Arnold connect the devil with death?

answers.summary: Arnold pointed to Hebrews 2:14 and discussed Apollyon and Abaddon as destroyer names. He also supplied Strong’s Greek number 622. These lexical identifications are reported as his explanation rather than an independently checked dictionary entry.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct a listener asking about kings of north and south?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to Daniel 11 and briefly associated its rulers with areas around Egypt and Iran. That geographic identification is his interpretation, not an independently established current political map.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct a listener asking about lewdness among condemned sins?

answers.summary: Arnold suggested Ezekiel 23, beginning around verse 21, as a possible passage. His recollection of the final verse was uncertain, so the proposed range is not presented as an exact verified citation.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct a listener asking about Midian before Genesis 37?

answers.summary: Arnold referred approximately to Genesis 25:2 and associated Midian with Abraham and his second wife. The wife’s name is corrupted in the captions and is not reconstructed. The surrounding same-tribe question remains held.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct a listener asking about Og’s large bed?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to Numbers 21:33 and said to trace Og onward from there. He did not identify the exact verse describing the bed in this reply; no additional citation is supplied as though he had spoken it.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct a listener asking about Paul’s account of persecution?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively recommended 2 Corinthians 6 and said it described suffering experienced by Paul and others. His probably is preserved rather than turning the reference into a definitive identification.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct a listener to read about Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Daniel 3 and describes their protection in the furnace. He also mentions Nebuchadnezzar’s account in Daniel 4.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct listeners about Michael, Satan’s restraint and his expulsion?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to Revelation 12 and described Michael and his angels casting Satan to earth. He connected the ensuing deception with the Spirit’s testimony through believers and Mark 13’s instruction not to premeditate their response.

questions.question: Where did Arnold direct listeners about obeying civil law?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Romans 13 and uses the ministry’s ability to broadcast under constitutional religious freedom as an illustration. This reports his argument, not an independent legal interpretation or current licensing assessment.

questions.question: Where did Arnold expect antichrist to appear and establish his claim?

answers.summary: Arnold said from the Mount of Olives and described a claim to divinity at Mount Zion, referring to 2 Thessalonians 2. He warned against neglecting Revelation or depending on assurances that believers would already be gone. These are his prophetic interpretations.

questions.question: Where did Arnold explain his belief that Jerusalem is God’s chosen dwelling?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Ezekiel 16’s city-as-woman imagery and its covenant, then connects it with the heavenly Jerusalem in Revelation 21. He uses the passages to describe God’s future dwelling.

questions.question: Where did Arnold find his teaching about flesh and spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the listener to 1 Corinthians 15, starting around verse 35. He uses the seed-and-plant analogy to explain his account of a spiritual body emerging when the flesh body dies.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate ammi and lo-ammi?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected the proposed book to Hosea and explained the names through my people and not my people, alongside compassion language. He described a symbolic relationship and restoration. His exact chapter placement for the reversal was not established in this answer.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate God’s promise not to destroy life by flood again?

answers.summary: Arnold pointed to Genesis 8:21 and 9:13, interpreting the rainbow as a reminder of God’s covenant, and mentioned Isaiah 54. He also made a climate claim about recent cooling; that broadcast-era assertion is not independently verified here.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate Jesus making a whip, and how certain was he about its form?

answers.summary: Arnold gives John 2:15 and explicitly says cat of nine tails is his added description, not the verse’s wording. He allows uncertainty about the number of cords.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate no weapon formed against you shall prosper?

answers.summary: Arnold gives Isaiah 54:17 and expresses confidence in God’s protection. This is his religious reassurance, not an individualized physical-safety guarantee.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate the account of a servant seeing God’s protecting army?

answers.summary: Arnold corrects the listener’s identification from Elijah to Elisha and points to 2 Kings 6:17. He describes the servant’s eyes being opened to see the protecting heavenly army.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate the statement that Moses’ burial place is unknown?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Deuteronomy 34 around verse 6 and says God buried Moses. He also mentions an uncertain additional reference and connects the account with his transfiguration interpretation.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate the teaching about being in the world but not of it?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to John 17:14 and Christ’s prayer to the Father, applying it to believers doing God’s work in this age.

questions.question: Where did Arnold locate the warning about failing to provide for one’s family?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to 1 Timothy 5:8 and paraphrased its warning as being worse than an infidel when a person refuses to care for their own family. He did not develop detailed exceptions or limits in this short reply.

questions.question: Where did Arnold place antichrist’s appearance within Matthew 24?

answers.summary: Arnold treated the earlier warnings as the building of a political system before the appearance, then pointed toward verse 9 and being delivered up. The listener’s verse numbers are unclear in the captions.

questions.question: Where did Arnold place the deadly wound within the five-month period?

answers.summary: Arnold placed the deadly wound in the middle of the five-month period. This specific sequence is kept distinct from broader five-month answers.

questions.question: Where did Arnold place the great white throne judgment?

answers.summary: Arnold places it on earth and connects it with God’s future dwelling described in Revelation 21. He rejects the assumption that such judgment requires a rapture into heaven.

questions.question: Where did Arnold place the nations omitted from his millennium temple illustration?

answers.summary: Arnold said the illustration did not show their places but the accompanying teaching did. He emphasized that God loves all his children and that people earn their places.

questions.question: Where did Arnold place the tribe of Levi among the other tribes?

answers.summary: Arnold says Levi is distributed among the tribes. The answer is brief and does not separately resolve every tribe count in the listener’s question.

questions.question: Where did Arnold point a listener seeking God’s promises in Isaiah?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Isaiah 43:26 and interprets reminding God as demonstrating knowledge of his promises. He encourages discussing those promises with God in prayer.

questions.question: Where did Arnold point for God’s ownership of earthly property?

answers.summary: Arnold cited Psalm 50’s description of God owning the cattle and hills and reasoned that the Creator owns what he made.

questions.question: Where did Arnold point for prayers kept before God?

answers.summary: Arnold cited Revelation 8:3–4 and said God hears, retains and receives the saints’ prayers, using vial or bottle imagery. This is the reference he gave; the wording is not silently moved to another passage.

questions.question: Where did Arnold say evil spirits should be sent?

answers.summary: Arnold said to order them in Christ’s name to return to where they came from, describing the wrong side of the gulf. He used the swine episode as an illustration and distinguished evil spiritual influence from the Holy Spirit. This is his religious explanation, not a diagnosis of a person’s experiences.

questions.question: Where did Arnold say Moses is now?

answers.summary: Arnold said Moses is with the Lord and appealed to his appearance at the transfiguration. The chapter number stated in the captions is uncertain and is not supplied as a verified reference.

questions.question: Where did Arnold say people who died before Christ went?

answers.summary: Arnold says they were in paradise and interprets 1 Peter 3–4 as Christ offering them salvation while his body was in the tomb. He also connects Ezekiel’s dry bones with spiritual teaching.

questions.question: Where did Arnold say the Tennessee excavation he discussed was located?

answers.summary: Arnold identified Bat Creek in Loudon County, Tennessee and said the stone was in the Smithsonian. He was uncertain about the excavation date and claimed a translation of the inscription. Those historical and translation claims are not independently verified; damaged wording in the proposed translation remains held.

questions.question: Where did Dennis direct a listener asking about the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jeremiah 4 and 2 Peter 3, interpreting them in terms of three heaven and earth ages. He distinguishes the end of an age from the end of time and recommends Arnold’s Three World Ages study.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate judgment beginning at the house of God?

answers.summary: Dennis cited 1 Peter 4:17 and applied it especially to teachers and ministers. He urged serious study and care not to mislead others.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the land of Nod?

answers.summary: Dennis uses the Euphrates and Tigris rivers mentioned in Genesis 2 to give the general location of Eden. He then points to Genesis 4:16 and locates Nod east of Eden.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the teaching about forgiving seventy times seven?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Matthew 18:21–22 and Peter’s question about forgiving a brother. He gives the number as 490, applies forgiveness to repentance, and explains repentance as a true change of heart and behavior. This answer retains his wording without treating it as identical to other answers about forgiveness limits.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for leaving parents and becoming one flesh in marriage?

answers.summary: Dennis pointed to Genesis 2:24: a husband leaves his parents, cleaves to his wife, and the two become one flesh.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for what goes around comes around?

answers.summary: Dennis referred to mischief returning on a person’s head and to reaping what one sows as biblical expressions of that idea.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point to Mary’s other children?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew 13, names James, Joses, Simon and Judas as Jesus’ half brothers, and distinguishes this Judas from Judas Iscariot. He says the following verse also mentions sisters without naming them.

questions.question: Where in Father's letter does it say old men will have minds of children?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor says the reference is likely Isaiah 3:4, where it states that babes shall rule, though the exact wording may differ.

questions.question: Where in the Bible can I find the Jesus prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says the exact prayer quoted by the listener is not in the KJV and directs him to Jesus’ model prayer to the Father in Matthew 6:9. He discourages repeating only a canned prayer and encourages speaking from the heart.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say how old Jesus was when he was crucified?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray states that the Bible does not explicitly state Jesus' age at crucifixion. However, he explains that Jesus was about 30 when he was baptized and began his ministry, and estimates he was 32 or 33 when he was crucified based on the number of Passovers celebrated.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say that it is a sin to lust after your own wife?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe Scripture forbids sexual desire toward one’s own wife. He distinguishes that from the indiscriminate lust he discusses in connection with Matthew 5:28.

questions.question: Where in the word does it tell us not to abstain from fellowship with other Christians?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: asked about fellowship, Dennis first discusses when to separate from people promoting teaching contrary to Scripture. He cites 2 Thessalonians 3:14 and 2 John 9–10. His response does not resolve every part of the listener’s separate question about attending a local church.

questions.question: Where is Satan now and when is he going to be turned loose?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes Satan’s evil spirit being active from Satan himself being restrained by Michael. He says Satan has five months after being cast from heaven, referring to Revelation 12 and 9. He identifies Satan’s role then as the false Christ; the five months are not placed before the expulsion.

questions.question: Where is the color amber found in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray states that amber is found in Ezekiel 1:4, where it describes the color of the vehicle that brought the throne of God to earth.

questions.question: Where the Bible does it say that Jesus was born on September 26th or 29th?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray suggests understanding the Course of Abia and recommends ordering Pastor Arnold Murray's CD, 'Christmas'.

questions.question: Where will the anti-Christ appear, and will he be in the flesh?

answers.summary: Dennis says the antichrist will be cast from heaven rather than born as a human. He infers an appearance on the Mount of Olives from the antichrist’s impersonation of Christ and says this precedes Christ’s return. His location argument is an inference in this answer.

questions.question: Which Apocrypha passage did Arnold say he liked to read?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended a Goodspeed edition and a passage captioned Ezra chapter 7 verse 77 for imagery of heaven. He explicitly distinguished enjoying it from teaching it as biblical authority and acknowledged that some Apocrypha material is questionable. The exact captioned citation is not silently standardized.

questions.question: Which Bible and tools did Arnold recommend for checking Hebrew meanings?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended the Companion Bible and Strong’s Concordance for checking English words against Hebrew meanings. He criticized the NIV and used his interpretation of Ezekiel 13 as an example; his paraphrase is not reproduced as a KJV quotation.

questions.question: Which Bible chapter did Arnold recommend for planting seeds?

answers.summary: Arnold said he used the whole Bible but particularly liked Mark 13 for explaining the elect’s destiny and the Spirit’s testimony before false Messiah. He did not require every witness to be a great scholar.

questions.question: Which book did Arnold recommend about Joseph of Arimathea and Jesus’ youth?

answers.summary: Arnold named Traditions of Glastonbury and described Joseph of Arimathea as Jesus’ uncle in that tradition. He connected it with tin trading, a voyage and early Christianity in Glastonbury. These are the traditions he recommended, not independently verified biography.

questions.question: Which book did Arnold recommend for learning to live well in flesh life?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Ecclesiastes as instruction for people living under the sun, including happiness, care of the body and learning from recurring human experience.

questions.question: Which book did Arnold recommend for witnessing to members of another church?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended the Bible as the book for witnessing truth. He declined to name the particular church and did not recommend an additional named handbook.

questions.question: Which Companion Bible cross-reference did Arnold propose correcting in this broadcast?

answers.summary: Arnold said the listener’s reported Psalm 88 marginal reference was a copyist error and proposed Psalm 44:22 instead. The attached page and edition are unavailable, so this is his suggested correction rather than an instruction to alter every edition.

questions.question: Which country did Arnold identify as the target of Russia in his prophetic interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished Judah from what he called true Israel and identified the latter with the United States. He expected a different judgment at Jerusalem. These are his historical and prophetic identifications, not verified geopolitical predictions.

questions.question: Which fish did Arnold call clean to eat?

answers.summary: Arnold specified fish with scales, cited Leviticus 11:12, and contrasted them with bottom-feeding scavengers. This summary preserves his stated criterion without adding another criterion he did not mention in this answer.

questions.question: Which kind of archaeology magazine did Arnold recommend for biblical study?

answers.summary: Arnold suggested a publication described in the captions as Biblical Archaeology and obtaining it through a magazine seller. The precise publication title is not clear enough to identify confidently.

questions.question: Which military formation did Arnold say he served with?

answers.summary: Arnold said he served with the First Marine Division on a special attachment near the northern reservoir. This records his recollection without supplying a more specific regiment not clearly given in the captions.

questions.question: Which of Arnold’s sons did he identify as older?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies Dennis as the elder and David as younger.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold compare with Saddam Hussein’s disheveled capture appearance?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected his recollection to Daniel 4:33 and compared Nebuchadnezzar with Saddam Hussein as a type involving Babylon. This is his historical analogy rather than proof of prophetic identity.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend about consulting mediums?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended 1 Samuel 28:7–8 and studying familiar spirits and witchcraft in Strong’s. He opposed seeking messages through mediums and said God could convey a message without them. His reference to an ancient penalty is not a call for private retaliation.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend about the apparent prosperity of the wicked?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the listener to Psalm 37 and its acrostic as explained in the Companion Bible. He reads the passage as warning of the wicked’s eventual destruction rather than lasting advantage.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend for a wedding service?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Matthew 19:6 and said he used it in wedding services.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend for someone entering police service?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Psalm 144 for a listener concerned about possible use of force in police service. He applied it to protection of the public and military service, not as a blanket legal authorization.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend to help children see a purpose in studying Scripture?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Mark 13, emphasizing purpose, a role in God’s plan and the Holy Spirit’s testimony. He suggested that seeing themselves addressed by Scripture would encourage the children to study. This is his pastoral application.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold suggest about people judging a marriage?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively suggested 1 Timothy 4:3 and opposed others judging marriage or food. He added an unclear qualification about marrying someone God created to be received. That limitation remains unresolved rather than expanded into a rule he did not explicitly explain.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold suggest for a rebellious spirit and bringing thoughts to God?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Luke 10:19, interpreting it as authority over evil spirits and Satan. He urged accepting that authority and anointing oneself and the home. He did not separately explain the listener’s phrase about taking every thought captive.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold use to explain chapter-by-chapter Bible study?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended 2 Timothy 2:15 and explained rightly dividing as attending to speaker or audience, subject, context and time period. He preferred sustained chapter-and-verse study to building an entire message around an isolated verse.

questions.question: Which passage did Dennis cite for Satan twisting Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis pointed to Matthew 4:6 and Psalm 91:11, using the temptation of Jesus to warn against a slight distortion of Scripture and deliberately testing God. His account is a paraphrase, not a substitute for the verses.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold give for a question about disciplining children?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the listener to Proverbs 13:24 and Hebrews 12. This brief answer supplies references in response to the listener’s question; it does not develop limits or practical methods of discipline.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold give for the continued existence of Israel’s scattered tribes?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected the reported claim that the people disappeared after AD 70. He cited Matthew 10:6 and James’s opening address to scattered tribes. This response supplied biblical references, not independent proof of the identity of modern nations.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold recommend to someone who regarded Jesus only as a dead prophet?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended John 14 and Isaiah’s Emmanuel prophecy to explain his understanding of Christ as God with us. He also connected Psalm 22 with the crucifixion and Psalm 23 with resurrection life; these are his applications.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis recommend for signs preceding Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis directed the listener to Matthew 24 and Mark 13 and recommended studying those chapters rather than giving a new date or list of contemporary predictions.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis use for 40-, 70- and 120-year generations?

answers.summary: Dennis cited Numbers 14:33 for forty years in the wilderness, Psalm 90:10 for seventy years, and Genesis 6:3 for 120 years. These are the passages he used for the three lengths in his teaching.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis use to place antichrist before Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis appealed to 2 Thessalonians 2’s apostasy and man of sin before the second advent, identifying the deceiver as Satan. He also referred to Isaiah 14’s throne and worship imagery. These are his prophetic identifications.

questions.question: Which Scripture did Arnold offer a listener concerned about distance from a disruptive relative?

answers.summary: Arnold refers to 2 Thessalonians 3:6 onward and reassures the listener. The saved question does not specify every action she has taken, so the answer is not generalized into approval of an unstated behavior.

questions.question: Which Strong’s Concordance edition did Arnold recommend in this broadcast?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended the version carried by the ministry and alleged fewer numbering errors than some other editions. He did not name a publisher or edition in this answer, and the reply does not establish current stock or comparative accuracy.

questions.question: Which tribe did Dennis identify as Samson’s?

answers.summary: Dennis identified Samson as a Danite through his father Manoah and directed the listener to Judges 13. The captioned question’s reference to Africa is uncertain; his answer clearly identifies the tribe of Dan.

questions.question: Which tribes did Arnold associate with Jesus’ ancestry?

answers.summary: Arnold described Jesus as having Judah’s royal line and Levi’s priestly line through his interpretation of Mary’s family. He referred to Luke 1 and connected the combination with Melchizedek.

questions.question: Which tribe’s standard did Dennis associate with Virgo?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Bullinger’s Companion Bible note on Numbers 2:7 and says it associates Virgo with the standard of Zebulun.

questions.question: Which verse did Arnold recommend when a change of heart feels difficult?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended 1 Corinthians 10:13 for reassurance about enduring trials and finding a way out. A nearby captioned sentence about never testing is incomplete, so it is not presented as a direct quotation or an unlimited promise.

questions.question: Which verse did Arnold suggest for a listener’s question about claiming to be without sin?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively suggested 1 John 1:8. The listener’s captioned wording refers to not lying, so his suggested reference is recorded as tentative rather than silently rewriting the question.

questions.question: Which verses did Dennis use when linking Cain with Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis cited John 8:44 and 1 John 3:12. He interpreted the people addressed in John 8 as descendants of Cain and identified the wicked one with Satan. These are his interpretive claims, not an independently established ancestry finding.

questions.question: Which women prophets did Arnold recommend studying?

answers.summary: Arnold named Huldah and Deborah and suggested looking up prophetess in Strong’s Concordance. He cited 2 Kings 22:14. His later identification of the father of four prophesying daughters is uncertain in the captions and is not corrected or endorsed here.

questions.question: Who besides the very elect did Arnold expect to overcome Antichrist?

answers.summary: Arnold said the listener had omitted the 144,000, whom he expected to recognize fulfilled prophecy after hearing the elect’s testimony. He also included kings and queens of the ethnic peoples who would overcome.

Arnold answered no, referring to kings and queens of the ethnic peoples and to Revelation 7’s innumerable group washed in the Lamb’s blood. He distinguished people already in heaven before Antichrist’s earthly deception.

questions.question: Who did Adam's son Seth marry?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray answered that Seth married one of Adam and Eve's other children, which was his sister, as incest laws were not given until later, during Moses' time.

questions.question: Who did Arnold credit for his understanding of the Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold credited years of study and research together with the Holy Spirit. He did not name a particular human teacher in this brief answer.

questions.question: Who did Arnold credit with assembling the Companion Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes God and the biblical writers from Bullinger’s editorial and study work. He praises the outlines and language helps. Biographical details he recalls, including a death year, are not independently verified and remain excluded as precise historical facts.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the Comforter, and did he say it is present now?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the Comforter as the Holy Spirit promised by Christ and received at Pentecost. He describes its help through Scripture, understanding and doing God’s work.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the disciple whom Jesus loved?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the disciple as John and associates him with the Gospel, the epistles of John and Revelation. He emphasizes John’s faithfulness and usefulness in recording the message.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the main writer of Psalms?

answers.summary: Arnold says David wrote most of Psalms.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the tree of life?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the tree of life symbolically with Jesus Christ and contrasts it with the tree he associates with Satan. He points to its presence in Genesis and Revelation and explains the tree imagery as metaphor.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the writer of Revelation?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes God as the source of Scripture from John as the scribe. He identifies John on Patmos as the person who recorded Revelation and associates him with the epistles of John.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say Cain feared after leaving Eden?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies them with peoples he reads as a sixth-day creation and relates the answer to Cain’s wife. This is his ancestry interpretation rather than established population history.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say can approach God or Christ in the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes approaching Christ during the millennium from approaching the Father afterward. He refers to Ezekiel 44 and the role of the elect as priests. Part of the listener’s wording is unclear even to the speaker.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say fights the final battles?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the final battles with Hamon-Gog and Armageddon and says God fights them. His political and national associations remain prophetic interpretations rather than established present-day identities.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say receives strong delusion in 2 Thessalonians 2?

answers.summary: Arnold applies the passage to people accepting the false Christ after rejecting the warning that the antichrist comes first. He connects it with the sixth and seventh trumpets and says ignorance does not make that worship acceptable.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as Israel’s twelve patriarchs?

answers.summary: Dennis identified the patriarchs as Jacob’s twelve sons and the fathers of Israel’s tribes, directing the listener to the blessings in Genesis 49.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as Nahum?

answers.summary: Dennis identified Nahum as the seventh minor prophet and associated his prophecy with Nineveh’s downfall.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as the rest of the dead in Revelation 20?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted the rest of the dead as people outside the first resurrection who had worshiped antichrist. He distinguished a spiritual body from a soul still liable to die and said the second death has no power over those in the first resurrection.

questions.question: Who did Dennis say God addressed in let us make man in our image?

answers.summary: Dennis answered that God was speaking to the angels. This is his interpretation of the plural wording.

questions.question: Who did Dennis say would teach and learn during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis said those who overcome antichrist would reign with Christ and teach others. He described the students as people who had not had an opportunity to hear truth before Christ’s return at the seventh trumpet.

questions.question: Who did God divorce?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor references Jeremiah 3:8, explaining that God divorced Israel because she, like Judah, was committing adultery symbolically through idolatry, worshiping other gods than the Heavenly Father, but God will take her back and make things right.

questions.question: Who was the woman that cast a piece of millstone on Abimelech's head and broke his skull wide open?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray says her name is not written, but she cracked Abimelech's head open like an egg. He ordered his servant to kill him to avoid being remembered as killed by a woman.

questions.question: Who were the men in the fiery furnace, and who was the fourth?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Daniel 3, corrects the listener’s count of seven men, and identifies Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego with the Son of God as the fourth. He treats their refusal to worship the image as a pattern for resisting the antichrist.

questions.question: Whom did Arnold identify as the nations’ kings and queens?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted the nations in Revelation 21 as gentile or ethnic peoples with their own leaders. He compared those leaders with the elect and said their people would listen to teachers from among them.

questions.question: Whom did Arnold identify as the witnesses of Isaiah 43:10?

answers.summary: Arnold applied the verse particularly to God’s elect. He also directed the listener to Isaiah 43:26 and encouraged prayer about God’s promises and study to understand them.

questions.question: Whom did Arnold mean by ethnos?

answers.summary: Arnold described ethnos as peoples outside the ten tribes in his interpretation and stressed that it was an honorable designation. He appealed to the nations being present in the concluding vision of Revelation. This is his definition and application in this answer.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as his and Arnold’s mentors?

answers.summary: Dennis named Arnold Murray as his mentor and Roy Gillespie as Arnold’s mentor. This is biographical attribution only; no teaching from Gillespie is introduced here.

questions.question: Why did Arnold ask listeners to submit only one or two broadcast questions at a time?

answers.summary: Arnold said a letter requiring more questions than could fit in a session might be set aside to avoid taking up the whole program. He recommended resubmitting a short letter or calling and explained that he did not have time to answer individually by mail. This describes that broadcast’s format.

questions.question: Why did Arnold call David a man after God’s own heart?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes David’s courage, experience protecting sheep, reliance on God against Goliath and the messianic lineage.

questions.question: Why did Arnold divide his five-month period into two halves?

answers.summary: Arnold connected Revelation’s symbolic hour with five months and its half-hour silence with half of that interval. He consequently described two periods of two and a half months. This records his prophetic interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold emphasize asking in Christ’s name?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished titles and different forms of the name from the importance of approaching the Father through Christ. He treated this as an expression of belief rather than resolving the question by counting the seventeen occurrences mentioned by the listener.

questions.question: Why did Arnold emphasize Jesus being called Son of David?

answers.summary: Arnold linked the title with recognizing the true Christ and his reading of Luke 3 as Mary’s genealogy through Nathan. He also described Mary as connected with Aaron and David. These genealogical details are his interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold encourage water baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold says Christ set an example through water baptism. He distinguishes the outward act from Christ’s forgiveness of sins.

questions.question: Why did Arnold interpret Ezekiel 28 as referring to Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes the protecting cherub, the language of creation and the judgment in Ezekiel 28:18–19. He relates that description to Satan and the son of perdition. This reports his reading of the passage.

questions.question: Why did Arnold recommend a civil marriage license?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended a legally recognized marriage and connected it with family protections and benefits. This records his dated pastoral rationale rather than legal advice about a particular family’s eligibility or current law.

questions.question: Why did Arnold recommend dedication rather than baptism for a baby?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended parents dedicating the child and themselves to Christian care. He described baptism as a choice a baby cannot make and pointed to Jesus being baptized as an adult. The captioned oil phrase is unclear and is not silently reconstructed.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Abram fought the king who had defeated other enemies?

answers.summary: Arnold said earlier helpful actions did not excuse the later taking of Lot and other captives and possessions. He applied the story to the danger of doing useful things while also violating God’s commands; some names and family terms in the captions are unclear.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Cain’s offering was not accepted?

answers.summary: Arnold assumes it was not firstfruits and adds his Cain-parentage interpretation. The assumption and theological claim are not presented as an independently established explanation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say doing right can remain difficult after accepting Christ?

answers.summary: Arnold described opposition after turning away from Satan and urged confidence in Christ’s power. He also advised leaving friendships that keep drawing the believer into bad habits rather than repeatedly forcing an unreceived message.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Egypt repeatedly featured in the biblical accounts named by a listener?

answers.summary: Arnold described Egypt as used in God’s purposes and as a place of safety for Jesus’ family under threat. A named servant is inaudible in the captions. His additional prediction and historical claim about Egypt’s continuous nationhood are attributed, not independently verified.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Elijah was taken without dying?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly agrees with the listener that this relates to Elijah returning in the end times. He does not give a separate supporting reference in that short answer.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Enoch was taken by God?

answers.summary: Arnold affirmed transfiguration and associated Enoch’s being taken with preaching against fallen angels. He appealed to Genesis and Jude within that interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say false teachers are able to continue?

answers.summary: Arnold places responsibility on people who teach or follow human traditions rather than Scripture. He connects the existence of false teaching with free will, personal accountability and God’s provision of Scripture for testing what is taught.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say fellowship with like-minded believers can feel spiritually stronger?

answers.summary: Arnold described believers’ shared love of God’s word as minds and spirits meshing, connected it with Christ’s presence among those gathered and anticipated continued fellowship in eternity.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God hardened Pharaoh’s heart?

answers.summary: Arnold said the events would reveal the living God rather than the various gods people worshipped. He emphasized God’s care for Egyptian people as well, though the wording of his recalled Exodus 7:5 explanation shifts between peoples.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God should be the judge?

answers.summary: Arnold said God knows people’s thoughts and cannot be deceived, so he can judge accurately. He contrasted that with human courts’ ability to make mistakes. He did not separately develop the child’s second question about why Satan impersonates God.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God still allows Satan to live?

answers.summary: Arnold described Satan’s continued existence as a test of people’s fidelity, using Job as an example. He said God gives believers power to resist and emphasized discipline and love for God and others.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Jesus used Son of Man?

answers.summary: Arnold explained the title as referring to Christ’s life in a human flesh body. He connected it with John 1’s account of the Word becoming flesh.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Jesus was crucified rather than Moses?

answers.summary: Arnold referred to Hebrews 2:14 and said Christ entered flesh and died to destroy death, which he identified with the devil.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Job received blessing again at the end?

answers.summary: Arnold said Job continued serving God and had done nothing to make him ineligible for renewed blessing. He emphasized Job’s patience and the lesson not to accept his friends’ uninformed accusations as God’s teaching.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Matthew 24:22 speaks of flesh being saved?

answers.summary: Arnold said people were still in flesh bodies and interpreted the shortened days as protection from a convincing false Christ. He contrasted the shortened period with seven years and said he expected the elect to withstand deception. These are his prophetic interpretations.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Matthew gives Joseph’s genealogy for Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold explains it through adoption and contrasts Matthew with his reading of Mary’s line in Luke 3. His royal and priestly ancestry conclusions remain his interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say olive oil was chosen for anointing?

answers.summary: Arnold associated the choice with his belief that olive oil was pure and beneficial to the body. His broad claims comparing fats and oils are not independently verified medical conclusions.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say people enter flesh life after his first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold said this life lets people choose whether to love God or Satan. He believed some elect volunteered to teach truth, but time ran out before he provided the requested biblical documentation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say people of different religions would bow when Christ returns?

answers.summary: Arnold said all would bow to the true Christ, with some ashamed because they had worshipped the false Christ first. He stressed studying the sequence of end-time events and described a subsequent millennium of teaching.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Revelation’s chapters and seals are not simply chronological?

answers.summary: Arnold described seals as truths to understand, trumpets as commands executed and vials as wrath. He interpreted the first white-horse rider as antichrist and made a cheap-fabric bow claim. These are his lexical and prophetic interpretations, not independently verified dictionary meanings.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Satan cannot postpone God’s plan indefinitely?

answers.summary: Arnold said Satan cannot choose to remain in heaven indefinitely and will be cast out when Michael acts. He also described Satan’s pride as sustaining his belief that he can change the outcome. One restraint phrase is inconsistent in the captions and needs audio checking; no exact release date is established here.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Satan was jealous of God?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly answers that Satan thought himself better than God. Time runs out before he separately develops why many angels followed him.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Satan would still try to deceive the elect?

answers.summary: Arnold said Satan believes he is capable of winning even the elect. He warned the listener not to underestimate Satan’s deceptive appeal rather than assuming he would avoid those who recognize him.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say some listeners were only recently hearing his Kenite teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold attributed that to lack of teachers and scholars and connected it with his interpretation of Revelation’s approved churches. His accusations about ancestry and religious groups are unverified doctrinal claims and do not establish modern people’s lineage.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say the Companion Bible does not print Christ’s words in red?

answers.summary: Arnold said it simply is not a red-letter edition. He recommended following the subject and speaker through its outlines and using a separate red-letter KJV if helpful.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say the rich man addressed Abraham rather than God?

answers.summary: Arnold said Abraham was the person the rich man saw embracing Lazarus across the gulf, so Abraham was the one he addressed. He connected Abraham with blessing many peoples.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say the two witnesses must die?

answers.summary: Arnold reasoned that the witnesses had not previously died and associated them with Elijah and Moses. He explicitly framed part of this as an assumption based on the transfiguration and said their resurrection would document Christ’s arrival.

questions.question: Why did Arnold think faithful first-age souls still entered flesh life?

answers.summary: Arnold said the elect entered flesh to guide and help others, while distinguishing groups with differing responses in his proposed first earth age. He linked divine intercession and prior justification with Romans 8 and Ephesians 1:4. These are his interpretations rather than verified accounts of prehuman existence.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Dan and Ephraim were omitted from Revelation 7’s list?

answers.summary: Dennis attributed the omission to idolatry, described Levi and Joseph as their replacements in that list, and said Dan and Ephraim were reinstated in Ezekiel 48.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God gave people the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis described it as instruction for how to live, follow God’s ways and receive his blessings.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Jacob could win his wrestling encounter with God?

answers.summary: Dennis says God allowed Jacob to win. He connects the encounter with Genesis 32:28 and the new name Israel, explaining the victory as something God permitted to make a point.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Satan is released after the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis explains the release as a test of whether God’s children will follow God or the devil. He points to Revelation 20, calls Michael the binding angel as his belief, and says some will follow Satan into the lake of fire. He distinguishes Satan’s later power from his role as antichrist.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the witnesses’ bodies would be left in the open?

answers.summary: Dennis affirmed Christ’s resurrection and said the exposed bodies would prevent a claim that someone stole the witnesses’ bodies. He expected their rising to be seen and connected it with Christ’s return.

questions.question: Why did God destroy the families and relatives of those who worshipped the golden calf, even though they did not participate?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the premise that Exodus 32 says innocent relatives were killed and quotes verse 33 about those who sinned. For the separate question about wartime bans, he refers to Deuteronomy 7:1–8 and interprets the destruction as preventing Israel from mixing with those peoples. This is an account of his reading, not a present-day instruction.

questions.question: Why did Jesus speak in parables?

answers.summary: Dennis says parables sometimes concealed meaning from the whole crowd while addressing disciples and the elect. He describes deeper meaning and notes that Jesus later explained some parables, including the sower in Matthew 13, to the disciples.

questions.question: Why do you always say if you have eyes to see and ears to hear?

answers.summary: Pastor Arnold Murray explains that having eyes to see and ears to hear refers to spiritual perception, not physical ability, emphasizing that many spiritually blind and deaf people have their spiritual eyes wide open.

questions.question: Why does Exodus 17 say Moses should strike the rock, but Numbers 20 say he should speak to the rock?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes Exodus 17 and Numbers 20 as separate events. He says Moses obeyed the command to strike the rock in the first and went wrong in the second when commanded to speak to it, speaking as though God needed his help. This summary is limited to the reviewed distinction.

questions.question: Why does God's mercy seat need protection from the likes of Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Ezekiel 28 as Satan having been assigned to protect the mercy seat but wanting to occupy it instead. He says that place belongs to Christ and gives this as his explanation for the protection imagery.

questions.question: Why is Cain not listed as a descendant of Adam?

answers.summary: Dennis says Cain is absent from Adam’s genealogy in Genesis 5 because, in his interpretation, Cain’s father was the serpent. He places Cain’s line in Genesis 4 and says Abel died before having offspring. These ancestry claims remain attributed to Dennis’s interpretation.

questions.question: Why would it take 1,000 years for the Lord's day, especially with spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray explains that if you take the thousand years literally, it might seem like a long time. However, in spiritual bodies, time has very little significance. He points to 2 Peter 3:8, where one day with the Lord is as 1,000 years, and 1,000 years as one day.

questions.question: Will a person remember the circumstances of death?

answers.summary: Arnold says God remembers and that the person does not forget the circumstances if they were known.

questions.question: Will angels be visible when they come?

answers.summary: Arnold answers yes, explaining that angels can be seen when present in the same dimension.

questions.question: Will God be upset with me if I forget what I learned due to my learning disability?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Luke 12:48 and says God knows people’s abilities and limitations. He expresses his belief that God values a disabled listener’s effort and explains that teachers are provided to help people learn. His reassurance does not require perfect recall.

questions.question: Will my husband be okay in paradise even though he didn't yet know that Satan comes to earth first?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the listener that if her husband died believing in Christ, he is saved. He distinguishes that from the danger of deception for people still living in flesh when the antichrist comes.

questions.question: Will our appearance resemble the alien pictures a listener sent?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the listener that people will not resemble the pictured spacemen. He appeals to Genesis 1:26 and says people look like those in whose image God made them.

questions.question: Will places like the mountains of Colorado be totally remade on earth in the end times?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray says God will remake the earth, wiping away tears and sorrow, and replacing all things with something much better, as described in Revelation chapter 21, verses 1-4.

questions.question: Will Satan be here before World War III or after?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not expect a World War III and stresses that Satan appears before Christ returns. This is his prediction in the recording, not an independently verified forecast.

questions.question: Will the four wheels found in Ezekiel one be our transportation in heaven? What will our transportation be?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the Ezekiel vehicle’s amber color as polished bronze and recommends Arnold’s Horses of the Bible study. He does not give a clear, detailed answer about the listener’s own future transportation; the recommendation is kept separate from such a promise.

questions.question: Will we be able to see our pets again after they have passed away? Please give me scripture from the Bible.

answers.summary: Dennis appeals to Isaiah 11:6 and interprets animals there as being in spiritual bodies. Asked whether people will see their pets, he says he believes so, retaining that qualification rather than presenting a guarantee.

questions.question: Will we be delivered before the two witnesses? Will we be delivered up before the two witnesses or after?

answers.summary: Dennis places being delivered up after the two witnesses have appeared and after the antichrist is present. He allows that the witnesses could still be teaching the elect while some are delivered, citing Revelation 11.

questions.question: Would Abraham have gone through with sacrificing his son, Isaac, had the angel of the Lord not stopped him?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks Abraham would have completed the sacrifice and points to Abraham’s faith in Hebrews 11. He treats the episode as a type of the sacrifice of God’s Son and emphasizes that the Lord provided the ram.

questions.question: Would the wine Jesus turned water to make a person drunk if abused?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray states that wine will make you drunk if you drink too much in a short period of time. He explains that the wine Jesus turned water to was most definitely fermented and therefore intoxicating.

questions.question: Would you explain the Scripture where He says, 'If you forgive not those that have wronged you, neither can God forgive you your trespasses,' in Mark 11:25-26.

answers.summary: Dennis Murray explains that forgiving others is necessary to be forgiven by God, but clarifies that forgiving does not mean forgetting. He emphasizes that forgiving someone who has wronged you takes time to rebuild trust, and that forgiving yourself is also important as God has already forgiven your sins. He warns that bringing up past sins repeatedly shows a lack of belief in God's forgiveness.
